definition.stemRaw:

You need to give Fabrikam users access to Contoso resources by using access packages. What should you use for each requirement?

blanks.label: Ensure that the Fabrikam users can use the access packages without explicitly creating guest accounts in contoso.com:
Allow non-administrative users in contoso.com to create the access packages by creating:

definition.explanation:
A connected organization identifies Fabrikam as an external Microsoft Entra directory for entitlement management, allowing its users to request access packages with their existing organizational identities; a guest identity is created when access is granted as needed. Catalog delegation supports non-administrative catalog creators, who can create access packages and policies.

**Learn more:** [Manage connected organizations in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-organization) · [Delegate access governance to catalog creators in entitlement management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/entitlement-management-delegate-catalog)

Catalog delegation supports non-administrative catalog creators, who can create access packages and policies.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription that includes a Microsoft Sentinel workspace.  
  
Your on-premises network includes firewalls that can forward event logs in the Common Event Format (CEF). No built-in Microsoft Sentinel connector exists for the firewalls.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to ingest firewall events into Microsoft Sentinel.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
definition.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel ingests CEF events from network and security appliances by using the CEF via Azure Monitor Agent connector with a Linux machine acting as a Syslog log forwarder. The on-premises Syslog server receives the firewalls’ CEF messages and forwards them for ingestion into the Sentinel workspace.

**Learn more:** [Ingest syslog and CEF messages to Microsoft Sentinel with the Azure Monitor Agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/connect-cef-syslog-ama?tabs=syslog%2Cportal) · [Syslog and Common Event Format (CEF) via AMA connectors for Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/cef-syslog-ama-overview)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Sentinel ingests CEF events from network and security appliances by using the CEF via Azure Monitor Agent connector with a Linux machine acting as a Syslog log forwarder. The on-premises Syslog server receives the firewalls’ CEF messages and forwards them for ingestion into the Sentinel workspace.

definition.stemRaw:
You need to recommend a SIEM and SOAR strategy that meets the hybrid requirements, the Microsoft Sentinel requirements, and the regulatory compliance requirements.  
  
What should you recommend?

blanks.label: Integrate Azure subscriptions by using:

Self-service sign-up user flows for Azure AD B2C

Azure Lighthouse onboards subscriptions for delegated cross-tenant management. Azure AD B2B and B2C self-service sign-up flows are identity features, not subscription-integration mechanisms.

**Learn more:** [Prepare for multiple workspaces and tenants in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/prepare-multiple-workspaces) · [Tenants, users, and roles in Azure Lighthouse scenarios](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/lighthouse/concepts/tenants-users-roles)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Sentinel workspaces are tied to Azure regions, so separate workspaces support geographic data-residency and regulatory requirements; tenant boundaries also require appropriate separation. Azure Lighthouse onboards subscriptions for delegated cross-tenant management. Azure AD B2B and B2C self-service sign-up flows are identity features, not subscription-integration mechanisms.

definition.stemRaw:
You have several on-premises Hyper-V hosts containing virtual machines that run Windows Server 2022, along with an Azure subscription.  
  
Recommend a solution for collecting Security event logs from the virtual machines by using Microsoft Sentinel. The solution must:  
  
- Use the Windows Security Events via AMA data connector.  
- Collect only specified events.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
What should you recommend?

blanks.label: In Azure, deploy:
options: Microsoft Defender for Cloud data collection settings

blanks.label: On the virtual machines, install:
blanks.answer: The Azure Connected Machine agent for Azure Arc-enabled servers
options: The Azure Connected Machine agent for Azure Arc-enabled servers
The VM insights Map Dependency agent on Windows

definition.explanation:
Windows Security Events via AMA uses Azure Monitor data collection rules to define event sets or custom XPath filters. Filtering at the agent to ingest only required events reduces data-ingestion costs. On-premises Windows Server virtual machines must be Azure Arc-enabled before an AMA-based Sentinel connector can collect their events; the Azure Connected Machine agent enables Azure Arc. The legacy Log Analytics agent is not the agent used by this connector.

**Learn more:** [Connect Microsoft Sentinel to other Microsoft services with a Windows agent-based data connector](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/connect-services-windows-based) · [Windows security event sets that can be sent to Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/windows-security-event-id-reference)

finalExplanation: Windows Security Events via AMA uses Azure Monitor data collection rules to define event sets or custom XPath filters. Filtering at the agent to ingest only required events reduces data-ingestion costs. On-premises Windows Server virtual machines must be Azure Arc-enabled before an AMA-based Sentinel connector can collect their events; the Azure Connected Machine agent enables Azure Arc. The legacy Log Analytics agent is not the agent used by this connector.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company intends to provision blob storage by using an Azure Storage account. The blob storage will be available to 20 application servers on the internet.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that ensures only the application servers can access the storage account.  
  
What should you recommend to secure the blob storage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: managed rule sets in Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) policies

choices.label: B
choices.text: inbound rules in network security groups (NSGs)

choices.label: C
choices.text: firewall rules for the storage account

choices.label: E
choices.text: service tags in network security groups (NSGs)

definition.explanation:
Azure Storage account firewall rules restrict access to the storage account’s public endpoint by allowed source IP addresses or IP ranges. Configuring rules for the public IP addresses of the 20 application servers permits their access and denies other internet sources.

**Learn more:** [Azure Storage firewall rules and network access control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-network-security)

finalExplanation: Azure Storage account firewall rules restrict access to the storage account’s public endpoint by allowed source IP addresses or IP ranges. Configuring rules for the public IP addresses of the 20 application servers permits their access and denies other internet sources.

definition.stemRaw:
You must recommend a solution to protect the `MedicalHistory` data in the `ClaimsDetail` table. The solution must satisfy the Contoso developer requirements.  
  
What should the recommendation include?
definition.explanation:
Always Encrypted protects sensitive column data by encrypting it on the client side and keeping plaintext encryption keys outside SQL Server or Azure SQL Database. A user who has database access but lacks access to the column master key cannot view plaintext values. Dynamic data masking is not sufficient for privileged database roles, including `db_owner`, because they can view unmasked data.

**Learn more:** [Always Encrypted with secure enclaves - SQL Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/security/encryption/always-encrypted-enclaves?view=sql-server-ver17) · [Dynamic Data Masking - SQL Server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/relational-databases/security/dynamic-data-masking?preserve-view=true&view=sql-server-ver17)

finalExplanation: Always Encrypted protects sensitive column data by encrypting it on the client side and keeping plaintext encryption keys outside SQL Server or Azure SQL Database. A user who has database access but lacks access to the column master key cannot view plaintext values. Dynamic data masking is not sufficient for privileged database roles, including `db_owner`, because they can view unmasked data.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You are designing a solution to protect confidential data in Microsoft SharePoint Online sites containing more than one million documents.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that prevents Personally Identifiable Information (PII) from being shared.  
  
Which two components should you include in the recommendation? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
definition.explanation:
Microsoft Purview DLP policies detect PII through sensitive information types in SharePoint Online content and can block external sharing when a rule matches. Sensitivity label policies publish labels that classify confidential content and apply protection settings such as encryption and access controls. Retention and eDiscovery capabilities address records management and investigation rather than preventing data sharing.

**Learn more:** [Help prevent sharing sensitive items via SharePoint and OneDrive with external users](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-ie/purview/dlp-create-policy-spo-odb-external) · [Enable sensitivity labels for files in SharePoint and OneDrive](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sensitivity-labels-sharepoint-onedrive-files)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Purview DLP policies detect PII through sensitive information types in SharePoint Online content and can block external sharing when a rule matches. Sensitivity label policies publish labels that classify confidential content and apply protection settings such as encryption and access controls. Retention and eDiscovery capabilities address records management and investigation rather than preventing data sharing.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company has a Microsoft 365 subscription and uses Microsoft Defender for Identity.  
  
You receive information about incidents related to compromised identities. You need to recommend a solution that exposes several accounts for attackers to exploit. When attackers try to exploit these accounts, an alert must be triggered.  
  
Which Defender for Identity feature should you recommend?
definition.explanation:
Honeytoken entity tags designate decoy accounts that serve as traps for malicious actors. Because honeytoken accounts are normally dormant, authentication associated with one triggers an alert in Microsoft Defender for Identity.

**Learn more:** [Entity tags in Microsoft Defender for Identity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-for-identity/entity-tags)

finalExplanation: Honeytoken entity tags designate decoy accounts that serve as traps for malicious actors. Because honeytoken accounts are normally dormant, authentication associated with one triggers an alert in Microsoft Defender for Identity.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription containing a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named MWS1 and an Azure Data Lake Storage account named lake1. Firewall log data is ingested into MWS1.  
  
You plan to export historical firewall log data from MWS1 to lake1.  
  
You need to make sure that security analysts can perform threat hunting from MWS1, including the firewall logs stored in lake1 in threat-hunting queries.  
  
What should you configure?

blanks.label: Microsoft Sentinel feature:
options: A Threat Intelligence Platforms data connector

definition.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel notebooks support programmatic investigation and threat hunting. The historical-data export notebook uses Azure Synapse to process the exported logs at scale, enabling analysis of data stored in Azure Data Lake Storage. Playbooks and Logic Apps connectors automate response workflows, while a Threat Intelligence Platforms connector ingests threat indicators rather than querying archived firewall logs.

**Learn more:** [Hunt for security threats with Jupyter notebooks - Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/notebooks-hunt) · [Export historical log data from Microsoft Sentinel](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftsentinelblog/export-historical-log-data-from-microsoft-sentinel/3413418)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Sentinel notebooks support programmatic investigation and threat hunting. The historical-data export notebook uses Azure Synapse to process the exported logs at scale, enabling analysis of data stored in Azure Data Lake Storage. Playbooks and Logic Apps connectors automate response workflows, while a Threat Intelligence Platforms connector ingests threat indicators rather than querying archived firewall logs.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy a storage account named storage1 to hold confidential data, and you will apply tags to that confidential data.  
  
You must ensure that access to storage1 can be defined by using the assigned tags.  
  
Which authorization mechanism should you enable, and which resource type should store the data?
definition.explanation:
Azure ABAC adds conditions to Azure role assignments and can evaluate resource attributes such as blob index tags. Azure Storage supports this tag-based authorization for Blob Storage, so confidential data requiring tag-based access conditions should be stored as blobs.

**Learn more:** [Authorize access to Azure Blob Storage using Azure role assignment conditions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-auth-abac) · [Tutorial: Add a role assignment condition to restrict access to blobs using Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/storage-auth-abac-cli)

finalExplanation: Azure ABAC adds conditions to Azure role assignments and can evaluate resource attributes such as blob index tags. Azure Storage supports this tag-based authorization for Blob Storage, so confidential data requiring tag-based access conditions should be stored as blobs.

definition.stemRaw:
You design cloud-based software-as-a-service (SaaS) solutions.  
  
You need to recommend a recovery solution for ransomware attacks. The solution must adhere to Microsoft Security Best Practices.  
  
What should you recommend doing first?
definition.explanation:
Microsoft ransomware guidance begins with preparing a ransomware recovery plan so the organization has a defined alternative to ransom payment and can restore access to systems and data. Data protection supports that plan, while privileged identity and access strategies are subsequent measures for limiting an attack’s impact.

**Learn more:** [Prepare for ransomware attacks with a backup and recovery plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/ransomware/protect-against-ransomware-phase1) · [Limit the impact that ransomware attacks can have](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/ransomware/protect-against-ransomware-phase2)

finalExplanation: Microsoft ransomware guidance begins with preparing a ransomware recovery plan so the organization has a defined alternative to ransom payment and can restore access to systems and data. Data protection supports that plan, while privileged identity and access strategies are subsequent measures for limiting an attack’s impact.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft 365 tenant.  
  
Recommend a Microsoft 365 Defender solution that improves tenant security and meets these requirements:  
  
- Identify users downloading an unusually large number of files from Microsoft SharePoint Online sites who could be attempting data exfiltration.  
- Block Microsoft Teams messages containing potentially malicious content by using zero-hour auto purge (ZAP).  
  
What should you recommend for each requirement?
definition.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps uses anomaly detection and user and entity behavior analytics to identify unusual multiple-file download activity in SharePoint Online, which can indicate data exfiltration. Microsoft Defender for Office 365 provides ZAP for Teams, which quarantines internal Teams messages later identified as malware or high-confidence phishing.

**Learn more:** [Create anomaly detection policies - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/anomaly-detection-policy) · [Microsoft Defender for Office 365 support for Microsoft Teams](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/mdo-support-teams-about)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps uses anomaly detection and user and entity behavior analytics to identify unusual multiple-file download activity in SharePoint Online, which can indicate data exfiltration. Microsoft Defender for Office 365 provides ZAP for Teams, which quarantines internal Teams messages later identified as malware or high-confidence phishing.

definition.stemRaw:
You plan to implement an Azure environment based on Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework enterprise-scale landing zone architecture principles. The environment will host three apps with these characteristics:  
  
- Each app will have development, test, and production environments.  
- A separate team will manage each environment.  
- Each app will store its secrets in Azure Key Vault.  
  
Recommend the number of Azure subscriptions and key vaults to deploy to the application landing zones.
definition.explanation:
Use one subscription for each application environment to isolate development, test, and production environments and let their separate teams manage their own scopes: 3 applications × 3 environments = 9 subscriptions. Use one Key Vault per application and environment to maintain secret isolation: 3 × 3 = 9 key vaults.

**Learn more:** [Manage application development environments in Azure landing zones](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/landing-zone/design-area/management-application-environments) · [Secure your Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/secure-key-vault)

finalExplanation: Use one subscription for each application environment to isolate development, test, and production environments and let their separate teams manage their own scopes: 3 applications × 3 environments = 9 subscriptions. Use one Key Vault per application and environment to maintain secret isolation: 3 × 3 = 9 key vaults.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing a ransomware response plan that adheres to Microsoft Security Best Practices.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that minimizes the risk that a ransomware attack will encrypt local user files.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
definition.explanation:
Protected folders, used with Microsoft Defender Controlled Folder Access, prevent untrusted applications from changing files in those folders. This directly blocks ransomware from encrypting protected local user files.

**Learn more:** [Configure controlled folder access (CFA)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/controlled-folder-access-configure) · [Demonstrate how controlled folder access blocks ransomware](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/defender-endpoint-demonstration-controlled-folder-access-ransomware)

finalExplanation: Protected folders, used with Microsoft Defender Controlled Folder Access, prevent untrusted applications from changing files in those folders. This directly blocks ransomware from encrypting protected local user files.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company uses an Azure App Service plan to deploy containerized web apps.  
  
You are designing a secure DevOps approach for deploying the web apps to that App Service plan. Recommend how to integrate code-scanning tools into a secure software development lifecycle. Scan the code during these two phases:  
  
- Uploading code to repositories  
- Building containers  
  
Where should code scanning be integrated for each phase?
definition.explanation:
GitHub Enterprise code scanning can run when code is pushed to a repository, identifying vulnerabilities at code-upload time. Azure Pipelines is the CI build environment, so security and container scanning tools can be integrated into the container build workflow before deployment.

**Learn more:** [GitHub Enterprise Cloud Docs — Code scanning](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud%40latest/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/code-scanning) · [Microsoft Learn — Secure your Azure Pipelines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/security/overview?nbsp=&view=azure-devops)

finalExplanation: GitHub Enterprise code scanning can run when code is pushed to a repository, identifying vulnerabilities at code-upload time. Azure Pipelines is the CI build environment, so security and container scanning tools can be integrated into the container build workflow before deployment.

definition.stemRaw:
You have two Azure subscriptions, **Sub1** and **Sub2**, that contain the vaults shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783896803445-0dt0srdc.png)  
  
You need to design a multi-user authorization (MUA) solution for security operations on the vaults. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- RSVault1 and RSVault2 must require MUA to disable soft delete, remove MUA protection, and disable immutability.  
- BackupVault1 and BackupVault2 must require MUA to disable soft delete and remove MUA protection.  
  
What is the minimum number of Resource Guard resources required?
definition.explanation:
A Resource Guard must be in the same Azure region as the Recovery Services vault or Backup vault it protects. Therefore, one Resource Guard can protect both East US vaults and a second can protect both West US vaults. Resource Guard supports the required mandatory protections for disabling soft delete and removing MUA protection, and can protect the optional immutability-disable operation for Recovery Services vaults.

**Learn more:** [Multiuser authorization using Resource Guard - Azure Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/multi-user-authorization-concept) · [Quickstart: Enable protection using Multi-user authorization in Azure Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/enable-multi-user-authorization-quickstart)

finalExplanation: A Resource Guard must be in the same Azure region as the Recovery Services vault or Backup vault it protects. Therefore, one Resource Guard can protect both East US vaults and a second can protect both West US vaults. Resource Guard supports the required mandatory protections for disabling soft delete and removing MUA protection, and can protect the optional immutability-disable operation for Recovery Services vaults.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription and an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to assess the existing environment to improve the overall security posture of these components:  
  
- Windows 11 devices managed by Microsoft Intune  
- Azure Storage accounts  
- Azure virtual machines  
  
What should you use to evaluate the components?
definition.explanation:
Microsoft 365 Defender (including Defender for Endpoint) provides device security posture and exposure assessment for managed Windows endpoints. Microsoft Defender for Cloud continuously assesses Azure resources and issues security recommendations for both virtual machines and Storage accounts.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for Endpoint security posture management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/security-posture-management) · [Microsoft Defender for Cloud recommendations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/review-security-recommendations)

finalExplanation: Microsoft 365 Defender (including Defender for Endpoint) provides device security posture and exposure assessment for managed Windows endpoints. Microsoft Defender for Cloud continuously assesses Azure resources and issues security recommendations for both virtual machines and Storage accounts.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription that includes multiple Azure Data Lake Storage accounts.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that encrypts the accounts’ content by using service-side encryption and customer-managed keys. The solution must ensure that individual encryption keys are applied at the finest-grained level.  
  
At what level should you recommend applying the encryption?
definition.explanation:
Azure Storage encryption scopes can be protected with customer-managed keys and applied to an individual blob. Because an Azure Data Lake Storage file is stored as a blob, applying the encryption scope per file provides the most granular key assignment. Container and account scopes apply one key to broader sets of data, and folders are not an encryption-scope level.

**Learn more:** [Encryption scopes for Blob storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/encryption-scope-overview) · [Azure Storage encryption for data at rest](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/azure/storage/common/storage-service-encryption)

finalExplanation: Azure Storage encryption scopes can be protected with customer-managed keys and applied to an individual blob. Because an Azure Data Lake Storage file is stored as a blob, applying the encryption scope per file provides the most granular key assignment. Container and account scopes apply one key to broader sets of data, and folders are not an encryption-scope level.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: For Azure SQL databases, recommend Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) that uses customer-managed keys (CMKs).  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure SQL Transparent Data Encryption uses an AES-256 database encryption key for encryption at rest. Customer-managed keys give the customer control over the TDE protector’s lifecycle, including rotation, and Azure SQL can automatically rotate to a newly enabled key version from Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM. This supports a monthly key-rotation schedule.

**Learn more:** [Customer-managed transparent data encryption (TDE) - Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, and Azure Synapse Analytics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/transparent-data-encryption-byok-overview?view=azuresql) · [Rotate TDE protector - Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, and Azure Synapse Analytics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/transparent-data-encryption-byok-key-rotation?view=azuresql)

finalExplanation: Azure SQL Transparent Data Encryption uses an AES-256 database encryption key for encryption at rest. Customer-managed keys give the customer control over the TDE protector’s lifecycle, including rotation, and Azure SQL can automatically rotate to a newly enabled key version from Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM. This supports a monthly key-rotation schedule.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: For blob containers in Azure Storage, you recommend encryption that uses Microsoft-managed keys in an encryption scope.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure Storage uses 256-bit AES encryption at rest, and encryption scopes support Microsoft-managed keys for containers and blobs. However, Microsoft-managed keys are rotated by Microsoft on its own compliance-based schedule; they do not support a customer-specified monthly rotation schedule. Specific rotation requirements require customer-managed keys.

**Learn more:** [Azure Storage encryption for data at rest](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-service-encryption) · [Create and manage encryption scopes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/blobs/encryption-scope-manage)

finalExplanation: Azure Storage uses 256-bit AES encryption at rest, and encryption scopes support Microsoft-managed keys for containers and blobs. However, Microsoft-managed keys are rotated by Microsoft on its own compliance-based schedule; they do not support a customer-specified monthly rotation schedule. Specific rotation requirements require customer-managed keys.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: For Azure SQL databases, recommend Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) using Microsoft-managed keys.  
  
Does this solution meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure SQL service-managed Transparent Data Encryption uses AES-256, but Microsoft rotates its built-in TDE certificates once per year. It does not provide a configurable monthly rotation schedule, so it cannot meet a requirement to rotate encryption keys monthly.

**Learn more:** [Transparent Data Encryption - Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, and Azure Synapse Analytics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/transparent-data-encryption-tde-overview?view=azuresql)

finalExplanation: Azure SQL service-managed Transparent Data Encryption uses AES-256, but Microsoft rotates its built-in TDE certificates once per year. It does not provide a configurable monthly rotation schedule, so it cannot meet a requirement to rotate encryption keys monthly.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: For Azure Storage blob containers, recommend encryption using customer-managed keys (CMKs).  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure Storage encryption uses 256-bit AES, and customer-managed keys can be stored in Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM. A Key Vault rotation policy can create new key versions monthly; when automatic key-version updating is configured, Azure Storage detects and uses the newest version. [Customer-managed keys for account encryption - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/customer-managed-keys-overview)

**Learn more:** [Customer-managed keys for account encryption - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/customer-managed-keys-overview)

finalExplanation: Azure Storage encryption uses 256-bit AES, and customer-managed keys can be stored in Azure Key Vault or Managed HSM. A Key Vault rotation policy can create new key versions monthly; when automatic key-version updating is configured, Azure Storage detects and uses the newest version. [Customer-managed keys for account encryption - Azure Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/customer-managed-keys-overview)

definition.stemRaw:
Your company has an office in Seattle.  
  
The company has two Azure virtual machine scale sets hosted on separate virtual networks. The company plans to hire contract developers in India.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that gives the developers the ability to connect to the virtual machines over SSL from the Azure portal. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Prevent the virtual machines’ public IP addresses from being exposed.  
- Provide the ability to connect without using a VPN.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
Which two actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a hub and spoke network by using virtual network peering.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deploy Azure Bastion to each virtual network.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deploy Azure Bastion to one virtual network.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Create NAT rules and network rules in Azure Firewall.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Enable just-in-time VM access on the virtual machines.

definition.explanation:
Azure Bastion provides browser-based RDP/SSH connectivity through the Azure portal while connecting to target virtual machines by private IP address, so the VMs do not require public IP addresses or a VPN. With virtual network peering, one Bastion host can connect to VMs in both its own VNet and a peered VNet; consolidating the deployment to one VNet minimizes Bastion cost.

**Learn more:** [VNet peering and Azure Bastion architecture](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/vnet-peering) · [Azure Bastion FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/bastion-faq)

finalExplanation: Azure Bastion provides browser-based RDP/SSH connectivity through the Azure portal while connecting to target virtual machines by private IP address, so the VMs do not require public IP addresses or a VPN. With virtual network peering, one Bastion host can connect to VMs in both its own VNet and a peered VNet; consolidating the deployment to one VNet minimizes Bastion cost.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company has a main office and 10 branch offices. Each branch office has an on-premises file server running Windows Server and multiple devices running either Windows 11 or macOS. The devices are enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You need to deploy Global Secure Access to provide web filtering for device traffic to the internet. The solution must ensure that all web traffic from devices in the branch offices is controlled by using Global Secure Access.  
  
What should you do first at each branch office?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure an Intune policy to onboard Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to each device.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure an IPsec tunnel on the router.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Install the Microsoft Entra private network connector on the file server.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure an Intune policy to deploy the Global Secure Access client to each device.

definition.explanation:
Global Secure Access remote network connectivity controls traffic for an entire branch by establishing an IPsec tunnel from the branch router or other on-premises network equipment to a Global Secure Access endpoint. The tunnel can route all internet-bound branch traffic through Global Secure Access for web-content filtering without requiring a client on every device.

finalExplanation: Global Secure Access remote network connectivity controls traffic for an entire branch by establishing an IPsec tunnel from the branch router or other on-premises network equipment to a Global Secure Access endpoint. definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant containing 10 Windows 11 devices and two groups named Group1 and Group2. The Windows 11 devices are joined to the Microsoft Entra tenant and managed by using Microsoft Intune.  
  
You are designing a privileged-access strategy based on the rapid modernization plan (RaMP). The strategy will include these configurations:  
  
- Each user in Group1 will be assigned a Windows 11 device configured as a privileged access device.  
- The Security Administrator role will be mapped to the privileged access security level.  
- Users in Group1 will be assigned the Security Administrator role.  
- Users in Group2 will manage the privileged access devices.  
  
You need to configure the local Administrators group on each privileged access device. The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
What should you include in the solution?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only add Group2 to the local Administrators group.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Configure Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (Windows LAPS) in legacy Microsoft LAPS emulation mode.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Add Group2 to the local Administrators group. Add the user that is assigned the Security Administrator role to the local Administrators group of the user's assigned privileged access device.

definition.explanation:
On a privileged access device, least privilege requires that the person who uses the device is NOT a local administrator, so they cannot weaken the hardened configuration. Microsoft's RaMP/privileged-access deployment guidance states that users of privileged workstations must have no administrator rights on their machines and sets "Additional local administrators on Microsoft Entra joined devices" to None. Only the team that manages the devices — Group2 — should be in the local Administrators group. Option C adds the Security Administrator (a device user from Group1) to their own device's local admins, which violates least privilege, so it is wrong.

**Learn more:** [Deploying a privileged access solution](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/privileged-access-workstations/privileged-access-deployment)

finalExplanation: On a privileged access device, least privilege requires that the person who uses the device is NOT a local administrator, so they cannot weaken the hardened configuration. Microsoft's RaMP/privileged-access deployment guidance states that users of privileged workstations must have no administrator rights on their machines and sets "Additional local administrators on Microsoft Entra joined devices" to None. Only the team that manages the devices — Group2 — should be in the local Administrators group. Option C adds the Security Administrator (a device user from Group1) to their own device's local admins, which violates least privilege, so it is wrong.

definition.stemRaw:

You plan to implement Azure Synapse Analytics SQL dedicated pools and SQL serverless pools.  
  
You need to recommend an additional encryption-at-rest security solution for each pool type. Use customer-managed keys whenever possible.  
  
What should you recommend for each pool type?

blanks.label: Serverless SQL pool:
blanks.answer: Azure Storage infrastructure encryption and Microsoft-managed keys
options: Azure Storage infrastructure encryption and Microsoft-managed keys
Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and customer-managed keys
Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and Microsoft-managed keys

blanks.label: Dedicated SQL pool:
blanks.answer: Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and customer-managed keys
options: Azure Storage infrastructure encryption and Microsoft-managed keys
Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and customer-managed keys
Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) and Microsoft-managed keys

definition.explanation:
Serverless SQL pools have no permanent SQL storage and rely on Azure Storage encryption; infrastructure encryption adds a storage encryption layer with Microsoft-managed keys. Dedicated SQL pools support TDE with a customer-managed TDE protector in Azure Key Vault, so this is the appropriate choice where customer-managed keys are available.

**Learn more:** [Azure Synapse Analytics security white paper: Data protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/synapse-analytics/guidance/security-white-paper-data-protection) · [Customer-managed transparent data encryption (TDE)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/transparent-data-encryption-byok-overview?view=azuresql)

finalExplanation: Serverless SQL pools have no permanent SQL storage and rely on Azure Storage encryption; infrastructure encryption adds a storage encryption layer with Microsoft-managed keys. Dedicated SQL pools support TDE with a customer-managed TDE protector in Azure Key Vault, so this is the appropriate choice where customer-managed keys are available.

definition.stemRaw:
To satisfy the application security requirements, which two authentication methods must the applications support? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.
definition.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Application Proxy supports SAML single sign-on for on-premises applications that consume Microsoft Entra-issued SAML tokens. It also supports integrated Windows authentication by using Kerberos Constrained Delegation, because those applications require a Kerberos ticket. NTLM cannot be used as an Application Proxy preauthentication or SSO method, and applications requiring client-certificate authentication are unsupported because Application Proxy terminates TLS.

**Learn more:** [SAML single sign-on for on-premises apps with Microsoft Entra Application Proxy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/app-proxy/conceptual-sso-apps) · [Kerberos Constrained Delegation for SSO with Microsoft Entra Application Proxy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/app-proxy/how-to-configure-sso-with-kcd)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Entra Application Proxy supports SAML single sign-on for on-premises applications that consume Microsoft Entra-issued SAML tokens. It also supports integrated Windows authentication by using Kerberos Constrained Delegation, because those applications require a Kerberos ticket. NTLM cannot be used as an Application Proxy preauthentication or SSO method, and applications requiring client-certificate authentication are unsupported because Application Proxy terminates TLS.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Bastion host and 100 Windows Server 2022 virtual machines. Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 2 is enabled on the virtual machines.  
  
Recommend a virtual-machine security solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- Administrators must request RDP access to the virtual machines through the Azure portal.  
- Remote Desktop sessions must be restricted to a maximum of three hours.  
- Agentless scanning must be scheduled for every virtual machine.  
  
What should you recommend using?

blanks.label: To manage RDP access:
options: The Login with Microsoft Entra option

blanks.label: To perform agentless scanning:
options: The Microsoft Defender for Cloud integrated Qualys vulnerability scanner

finalExplanation: Just-in-time (JIT) VM access is the Defender for Cloud feature that keeps management ports closed and requires administrators to request RDP access through the Azure portal, granting time-bound access with a configurable maximum duration (default three hours), which meets both the request-through-portal and three-hour limit requirements. For agentless scanning the correct engine is Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management: agentless machine scanning in Defender for Servers Plan 2 takes disk snapshots and analyzes them with integrated Defender Vulnerability Management, with no agent installed. definition.stemRaw:

You have an Azure subscription containing an Azure Virtual Desktop environment. The environment has host pools that use a custom golden image. Every Azure Virtual Desktop deployment belongs to one Microsoft Entra Domain Services domain.  
  
Recommend a way to deploy Microsoft Defender for Endpoint to the hosts that meets these requirements:  
  
- Hosts are onboarded to Defender for Endpoint during their first startup sequence.  
- The Microsoft Defender portal has one entry for every deployed VDI host.  
- Administrative effort is minimized.  
  
What should you recommend?

blanks.label: For the VDI:
blanks.answer: Add the Defender for Endpoint onboarding script to the virtual machine template.
options: Add the Defender for Endpoint onboarding script to the virtual machine template.
Deploy Defender for Endpoint by using a custom Group Policy Object (GPO).
Onboard the virtual machine template to Defender for Endpoint.

blanks.label: For Azure Virtual Desktop:
blanks.answer: Add the Defender for Endpoint onboarding script to the golden image.
options: Add the Defender for Endpoint onboarding script to the golden image.

Onboard the golden image to Defender for Endpoint.

definition.explanation:
For non-persistent VDI clones, the template must remain unonboarded because clones would inherit its Defender for Endpoint identity. The VDI onboarding scripts are placed in the template and run as startup scripts after the clone receives its final hostname, supporting a single device entry. For Azure Virtual Desktop, Microsoft recommends adding and configuring the onboarding script in the golden image so each provisioned host runs it at first boot; the golden image itself must not be onboarded.

**Learn more:** [Onboard non-persistent virtual desktop infrastructure (VDI) devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-endpoints-vdi) · [Onboard Windows devices in Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/onboard-windows-multi-session-device)

The VDI onboarding scripts are placed in the template and run as startup scripts after the clone receives its final hostname, supporting a single device entry. For Azure Virtual Desktop, Microsoft recommends adding and configuring the onboarding script in the golden image so each provisioned host runs it at first boot; the golden image itself must not be onboarded.

definition.stemRaw:

Standard V2 is intended for production workloads and supports the required product and policy model; Consumption does not support the flexible rate-limit-by-key policy.

**Learn more:** [Azure API Management key concepts](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-key-concepts) · [Azure API Management rate-limit policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/rate-limit-policy)

finalExplanation: API Management products bundle APIs and subscriptions control which developer groups can use each bundle. A rate-limit policy at product scope applies the limit to the APIs in that product, allowing separate limits per API set with less duplicated configuration than API-scoped policies. Standard V2 is intended for production workloads and supports the required product and policy model; Consumption does not support the flexible rate-limit-by-key policy.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to mitigate ransomware attacks against messages posted to Microsoft Teams channels and files stored in Teams channels.  
  
What should the solution include for each content type?

finalExplanation: Teams channel messages are stored in hidden Exchange Online mailboxes, and Teams channel files are stored in SharePoint/OneDrive, so each content type is protected by the native controls of its backing service. For messages, Exchange Online Protection (EOP) scans content and attachments in real time and deletes items containing known or suspected malware/ransomware, which is the ransomware mitigation Microsoft documents for Exchange-backed data; the Preservation Hold library is a SharePoint files construct and does not apply to messages, and Single Item Recovery only recovers deleted mail items rather than mitigating ransomware. For files, Files Restore lets you roll a SharePoint/OneDrive library back to a known-good point in time within the last 30 days, directly recovering from an encryption event, whereas Litigation Hold and the Preservation Hold library are retention/eDiscovery mechanisms, not point-in-time restore tools.

definition.stemRaw:

The company intends to use the following storage workloads:  
  
- Azure Storage blob containers  
- Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2

finalExplanation: Azure Blob Storage supports Microsoft Entra ID authentication through OAuth tokens and Azure RBAC. Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 supports Microsoft Entra ID identities for RBAC and ACL-based authorization because it is implemented on Azure Blob Storage. Azure Disk Storage does not provide this data-access authentication model.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company plans to migrate all on-premises virtual machines to Azure.  
  
A network engineer proposes the Azure virtual network design shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783809805078-7i9zsyy7.jpg)  
  
You need to recommend an Azure Bastion deployment that provides secure remote access to all virtual machines.  
  
Based on the virtual network design, how many Azure Bastion subnets are required?
definition.explanation:
An Azure Bastion host provides RDP/SSH access to virtual machines in its own virtual network and in directly peered virtual networks. A Bastion deployment in Hub VNet can serve Hub VNet, VNet1, and VNet2; a second deployment in either VNet3 or VNet4 can serve both of those peered virtual networks. Because the two peering groups are disconnected, two dedicated AzureBastionSubnet subnets are required.

**Learn more:** [VNet peering and Azure Bastion architecture](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bastion/vnet-peering)

finalExplanation: An Azure Bastion host provides RDP/SSH access to virtual machines in its own virtual network and in directly peered virtual networks. A Bastion deployment in Hub VNet can serve Hub VNet, VNet1, and VNet2; a second deployment in either VNet3 or VNet4 can serve both of those peered virtual networks. Because the two peering groups are disconnected, two dedicated AzureBastionSubnet subnets are required.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant called contoso.onmicrosoft.com and an Azure subscription called Sub1.  
  
You need to implement Microsoft Entra Verified ID by using Quick Verified ID setup.  
  
What should you create first?

choices.label: C
choices.text: a user-assigned managed identity in Sub1

choices.label: D
choices.text: an Azure key vault in Sub1

definition.explanation:
Quick Verified ID setup requires a custom domain registered in the Microsoft Entra tenant; without one, Quick setup is unavailable and the tenant defaults to the advanced setup experience. You have a Microsoft Entra tenant containing a security group named Group1. Group1 includes your company's IT support team members.  
  
Your Azure subscription has 800 Microsoft Entra joined Windows devices and 200 Microsoft Entra registered Windows devices. You also have 200 standalone macOS devices.  
  
You deploy 10 Microsoft Entra joined Windows devices and set Microsoft Entra ExtensionAttribute1 to `SecureWorkstation`.  
  
Recommend a Conditional Access solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- Allow access to Microsoft Entra resources only from devices that run Windows 10 or Windows 11.  
- Restrict Windows Azure Service Management API access for Group1 members to users who authenticate with multifactor authentication (MFA) and connect from a device with the `SecureWorkstation` ExtensionAttribute1.  
  
The solution must minimize the number of required policies while maximizing security.  
  
What should the recommendation include?

blanks.label: Device filters:
options: One include device filter and one exclude device filter

definition.explanation:
Use block policies with exclude device filters to enforce the device restrictions. Excluding the Windows 10/11 filter from a broad block policy allows those matching devices and blocks nonmatching devices. Excluding the `SecureWorkstation` filter from a block policy for Group1 and the Windows Azure Service Management API blocks the API from all other devices. MFA requires its own Conditional Access policy with an MFA grant control, because a block control cannot be combined to create an MFA exception. This requires three policies and two exclude device filters.

**Learn more:** [Filter for devices as a condition in Conditional Access policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-condition-filters-for-devices)

finalExplanation: Use block policies with exclude device filters to enforce the device restrictions. Excluding the Windows 10/11 filter from a broad block policy allows those matching devices and blocks nonmatching devices. Excluding the `SecureWorkstation` filter from a block policy for Group1 and the Windows Azure Service Management API blocks the API from all other devices. MFA requires its own Conditional Access policy with an MFA grant control, because a block control cannot be combined to create an MFA exception. This requires three policies and two exclude device filters.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Privileged Identity Management (PIM)

definition.explanation:
Preventive controls stop attacks before they happen, and both of these raise the Defender for Cloud secure score. Azure Web Application Firewall (A) blocks web-layer attacks and maps to secure-score controls such as "Protect applications against DDoS attacks." Privileged Identity Management (B) enforces just-in-time, time-bound privileged access and least privilege, feeding the identity/"Manage access and permissions" recommendations. Microsoft Sentinel (C) is a SIEM and Microsoft Defender for Cloud alerts (E) are detective/response controls, not preventive, so they are excluded. Azure Firewall is also preventive, but the pairing that this item tests as complete preventive solutions is WAF plus PIM.

**Learn more:** [Secure score in Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/secure-score-security-controls)

finalExplanation: Preventive controls stop attacks before they happen, and both of these raise the Defender for Cloud secure score. Azure Web Application Firewall (A) blocks web-layer attacks and maps to secure-score controls such as "Protect applications against DDoS attacks." Privileged Identity Management (B) enforces just-in-time, time-bound privileged access and least privilege, feeding the identity/"Manage access and permissions" recommendations. Microsoft Sentinel (C) is a SIEM and Microsoft Defender for Cloud alerts (E) are detective/response controls, not preventive, so they are excluded. definition.stemRaw:
Your company has offices in New York City and London. The London office hosts an on-premises application named App1.  
  
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant named contoso.com that is hosted in North America.  
  
You plan to manage London users’ access to App1 by using Microsoft Entra Private Access. In the London office, you will deploy Private Access by doing the following:  
  
- Deploy Microsoft Entra application proxy connectors.  
- Provision an ExpressRoute circuit at the nearest peering location.  
  
You need to optimize the network for this deployment. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Maximize connectivity redundancy for App1.  
- Minimize latency when App1 is accessed.  
- Maximize security.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
What should the solution include?

blanks.label: To optimize the connection between the users and the application proxy, deploy:
blanks.answer: Two connectors to a new connector group
options: A connector to the default connector group and a connector to a new connector group
Two connectors to a new connector group
Two connectors to the default connector group

blanks.label: To optimize the connection between the application proxy and the connectors, use:
blanks.answer: ExpressRoute with Microsoft peering and the premium add-on
options: ExpressRoute with Microsoft peering and the premium add-on

finalExplanation: For App1 you should create a dedicated (new) connector group in the London office and place at least two connectors in it: the dedicated group lets you pin the app to connectors physically near it (minimizing latency) while two connectors provide the required redundancy, which reusing the default group would not guarantee. The connectors reach the Application Proxy cloud service over Microsoft public endpoints, so Microsoft peering is required (private peering is only for Azure VNet private IPs and does not carry Application Proxy/Entra service traffic). Because the ExpressRoute circuit is provisioned at the nearest (European) peering location while the contoso.com tenant and its Application Proxy service instances live in North America, the traffic crosses geopolitical regions; standard ExpressRoute Microsoft peering only reaches Microsoft resources in the circuit's own region, so the premium add-on is needed for that global cross-region connectivity.

A Conditional Access policy named Policy1 allows only workload identities from trusted locations to access SharePoint Online.  
  
You plan to move all business-sensitive information to Site1. You need to ensure that CAPolicy1 applies only to Site1.  
  
Which three actions should you perform, in sequence?  
  
More than one ordering of the answer choices is valid; any correct ordering receives credit.

slots.answer: For the Microsoft Entra tenant, create an authentication context.
Modify the target resources of Policy1.
Configure a sensitivity label for Site1.

items: Modify the target resources of Policy1.
For the Microsoft Entra tenant, create an authentication strength.
For the Microsoft Entra tenant, create an authentication context.
Configure a sensitivity label for Site1.
definition.explanation:
An authentication context enables Microsoft Entra Conditional Access to be applied at the SharePoint-site level. Policy1 must target that authentication context rather than the SharePoint Online cloud app, and a sensitivity label assigned to Site1 applies the authentication context to that site. Authentication strength is unrelated to limiting the policy to one site.

finalExplanation: An authentication context enables Microsoft Entra Conditional Access to be applied at the SharePoint-site level. Policy1 must target that authentication context rather than the SharePoint Online cloud app, and a sensitivity label assigned to Site1 applies the authentication context to that site. Authentication strength is unrelated to limiting the policy to one site.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a hybrid Azure AD tenant with pass-through authentication enabled.  
  
You are designing an identity security strategy.  
  
You need to reduce the impact of brute-force password attacks and leaked credentials affecting hybrid identities.  
  
Each feature can be used once, more than once, or not at all.
definition.explanation:
Smart Lockout / Extranet Smart Lockout tracks failed sign-ins and locks out attackers after a threshold while distinguishing genuine users, which directly reduces the impact of brute-force and password-spray attacks; it is supported with pass-through authentication and shields on-premises AD accounts. Detecting leaked credentials for hybrid identities in Microsoft Entra ID Protection requires Password hash synchronization to be enabled, because Microsoft compares synced password hashes against known-breached credential sets. Azure AD Password Protection only bans weak/common passwords, so it does not address account lockout for brute force nor leaked-credential detection, and is left unused. Hence brute force maps to Smart Lockout and leaked credentials to password hash synchronization.

**Learn more:** [Prevent attacks using smart lockout](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-password-smart-lockout)

finalExplanation: Smart Lockout / Extranet Smart Lockout tracks failed sign-ins and locks out attackers after a threshold while distinguishing genuine users, which directly reduces the impact of brute-force and password-spray attacks; it is supported with pass-through authentication and shields on-premises AD accounts. Detecting leaked credentials for hybrid identities in Microsoft Entra ID Protection requires Password hash synchronization to be enabled, because Microsoft compares synced password hashes against known-breached credential sets. Azure AD Password Protection only bans weak/common passwords, so it does not address account lockout for brute force nor leaked-credential detection, and is left unused. Hence brute force maps to Smart Lockout and leaked credentials to password hash synchronization.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure Storage account named storage1.  
  
You intend to secure storage1 with a Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) approach.  
  
You create an Azure key vault named AKV1 and upload a compatible key.  
  
You need to configure storage1 to use the key stored in AKV1 for encryption.  
  
Which three actions should you perform, in sequence?

slots.answer: Create a managed identity and assign it to storage1.
Create and assign a Key Vault access policy.
Configure Azure Storage encryption with customer-managed keys.

items: Assign storage1 the Key Vault Reader role to access the key.
Create and assign an access policy for storage1.
Create a managed identity and assign it to AKV1.
Create a managed identity and assign it to storage1.
Create and assign a Key Vault access policy.
Configure Azure Storage encryption with customer-managed keys.
definition.explanation:
Azure Storage uses a managed identity to authenticate to Azure Key Vault when a customer-managed key is used. That identity must be assigned to the storage account and granted a Key Vault access policy with the required key permissions before the storage account can be configured to use the vault key. The Key Vault Reader role provides management-plane read access and does not grant cryptographic key operations.

**Learn more:** [Customer-managed keys for Azure Storage encryption](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/customer-managed-keys-overview) · [Configure customer-managed keys for an Azure Storage account](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/customer-managed-keys-configure-key-vault)

finalExplanation: Azure Storage uses a managed identity to authenticate to Azure Key Vault when a customer-managed key is used. That identity must be assigned to the storage account and granted a Key Vault access policy with the required key permissions before the storage account can be configured to use the vault key. The Key Vault Reader role provides management-plane read access and does not grant cryptographic key operations.

definition.stemRaw:

The Azure subscription contains 50 virtual machines. Each virtual machine runs distinct applications on Windows Server 2019.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that ensures only authorized applications can run on the virtual machines. If an unauthorized application tries to run or be installed, it must be blocked automatically until an administrator authorizes it.  
  
Which security control should you recommend?

choices.label: A
choices.text: adaptive application controls in Defender for Cloud

choices.label: B
choices.text: app protection policies in Microsoft Endpoint Manager

choices.label: C
choices.text: app discovery anomaly detection policies in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps

choices.label: D

definition.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud adaptive application controls analyze the applications running on virtual machines, generate an allow list of known-safe applications, and can enforce application-control policies so that unapproved software is prevented from executing. App protection policies protect data in managed mobile apps; Defender for Cloud Apps discovery policies address cloud-service use; and Azure Security Benchmark controls assess security posture rather than enforce a VM application allow list.

**Learn more:** [Azure security baseline for Windows virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/baselines/virtual-machines-windows-virtual-machines-security-baseline?context=%2Fpartner-support%2Fazure%2Fbackup%2Fcontext%2Fcontext) · [Microsoft Defender for Cloud compute security recommendations reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/recommendations-reference-compute)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud adaptive application controls analyze the applications running on virtual machines, generate an allow list of known-safe applications, and can enforce application-control policies so that unapproved software is prevented from executing. App protection policies protect data in managed mobile apps; Defender for Cloud Apps discovery policies address cloud-service use; and Azure Security Benchmark controls assess security posture rather than enforce a VM application allow list.

definition.stemRaw:
A customer uses the Zero Trust model and explicitly verifies every attempt to access its corporate applications.  
  
The customer identifies malware infections on several endpoints and suspends access attempts from those infected endpoints. The malware is subsequently removed from the endpoints.  
  
Which two conditions must be satisfied before endpoint users can again access the corporate applications? Each correct answer is part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: The client access tokens are refreshed.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Microsoft Intune reports the endpoints as compliant.

choices.label: C
choices.text: A new Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Conditional Access policy is enforced.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint reports the endpoints as compliant.

definition.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Endpoint must show that the remediated endpoints no longer have device risk, and Microsoft Intune must reassess them as compliant. Intune communicates device compliance to Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, which permits access once the threat is removed and the device is compliant.

**Learn more:** [Enable Conditional Access to better protect users and enterprise information](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/conditional-access) · [Integrate Microsoft Defender for Endpoint with Intune for Device Compliance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/overview)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint must show that the remediated endpoints no longer have device risk, and Microsoft Intune must reassess them as compliant. Intune communicates device compliance to Microsoft Entra Conditional Access, which permits access once the threat is removed and the device is compliant.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant that synchronizes with an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain.  
  
You have an on-premises datacenter containing 100 servers. The servers run Windows Server and are backed up by using Microsoft Azure Backup Server (MABS).  
  
You are designing a recovery solution for ransomware attacks. The solution adheres to Microsoft Security Best Practices.  
  
You need to ensure that a compromised local administrator account cannot be used to stop scheduled backups.  
  
What should you do?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From Azure Backup, configure multi-user authorization by using Resource Guard.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management (PIM), create a role assignment for the Backup Contributor role.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From Microsoft Azure Backup Setup, register MABS with a Recovery Services vault.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From a Recovery Services vault, generate a security PIN for critical operations.

definition.explanation:
Azure Backup multi-user authorization uses a Resource Guard to require separate authorization for critical, high-impact backup operations. This additional approval boundary helps prevent a single compromised administrator account from stopping or altering protected backups, which is a key ransomware-resilience control for MABS hybrid backups.

**Learn more:** [Configure Multi-user authorization using Resource Guard in Azure Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/multi-user-authorization) · [Security features that protect hybrid backups](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-security-feature)

finalExplanation: Azure Backup multi-user authorization uses a Resource Guard to require separate authorization for critical, high-impact backup operations. This additional approval boundary helps prevent a single compromised administrator account from stopping or altering protected backups, which is a key ransomware-resilience control for MABS hybrid backups.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure AD tenant synchronized with an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain. Client computers run Windows and are hybrid-joined to Azure AD.  
  
You are designing an endpoint-protection strategy against ransomware that follows Microsoft Security Best Practices.  
  
You plan to remove every domain account from the Administrators groups on the Windows computers.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that gives users administrative access to the Windows computers only when it is needed. The solution must minimize ransomware lateral movement if an administrator account on a computer is compromised.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
definition.explanation:
Windows LAPS manages and regularly rotates local administrator passwords, allowing authorized personnel to retrieve a device-specific local credential only for required administrative tasks. Device-unique local administrator passwords prevent a compromised password hash or credential from being reused against other endpoints, reducing pass-the-hash and lateral-traversal risk. Windows LAPS supports hybrid-joined devices.

**Learn more:** [Windows LAPS overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/identity/laps/laps-overview) · [Local accounts — Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/identity-protection/access-control/local-accounts)

finalExplanation: Windows LAPS manages and regularly rotates local administrator passwords, allowing authorized personnel to retrieve a device-specific local credential only for required administrative tasks. Device-unique local administrator passwords prevent a compromised password hash or credential from being reused against other endpoints, reducing pass-the-hash and lateral-traversal risk. Windows LAPS supports hybrid-joined devices.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company has an on-premises network in Seattle and an Azure subscription. The on-premises network includes a Remote Desktop server.  
  
The company contracts a third-party development firm in France to develop and deploy resources to the virtual machines hosted in the Azure subscription.  
  
Currently, the firm connects by RDP to the Remote Desktop server. From that Remote Desktop connection, the firm accesses the virtual machines hosted in Azure by using custom administrative tools installed on the Remote Desktop server. All traffic to the Remote Desktop server is captured by a firewall, which allows only specific connections from France to the server.  
  
You need to recommend a modern security solution based on the Zero Trust model. The solution must minimize latency for developers.  
  
Which three actions should you recommend? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Configure network security groups (NSGs) to allow access from only specific logical groupings of IP address ranges.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deploy a Remote Desktop server to an Azure region located in France.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Migrate from the Remote Desktop server to Azure Virtual Desktop.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Implement Azure Firewall to restrict host pool outbound access.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Configure Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Conditional Access with multi-factor authentication (MFA) and named locations.

definition.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop provides a managed Azure-based desktop access model, while Microsoft Entra Conditional Access can require MFA and apply location-aware access controls to verify external users explicitly. Azure Firewall can control and restrict outbound traffic from Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts, supporting segmentation and an assume-breach posture. These controls provide identity-based access and restricted workload egress without retaining the on-premises Remote Desktop server as the developer access path.

**Learn more:** [Apply Zero Trust principles to Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/azure-infrastructure-avd) · [Security recommendations for Azure Virtual Desktop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/security-recommendations)

finalExplanation: Azure Virtual Desktop provides a managed Azure-based desktop access model, while Microsoft Entra Conditional Access can require MFA and apply location-aware access controls to verify external users explicitly. Azure Firewall can control and restrict outbound traffic from Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts, supporting segmentation and an assume-breach posture. These controls provide identity-based access and restricted workload egress without retaining the on-premises Remote Desktop server as the developer access path.

You need to recommend a solution to the application development team to protect the application against identity-related attacks.  
  
Which two configurations should you recommend? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
> **NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Azure AD Conditional Access integration with user flows and custom policies

choices.label: B
choices.text: smart account lockout in Azure AD B2C

choices.label: D
choices.text: custom resource owner password credentials (ROPC) flows in Azure AD B2C

Smart account lockout mitigates credential attacks by locking accounts after repeated failed sign-in attempts, helping defend against brute-force and password-spray attempts.

**Learn more:** [Add Conditional Access to a user flow in Azure AD B2C](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory-b2c/conditional-access-user-flow) · [Mitigate credential attacks in Azure AD B2C with smart lockout](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory-b2c/threat-management)

finalExplanation: Azure AD B2C Conditional Access can integrate with user flows and custom policies to evaluate risky sign-ins and block access or require remediation such as multifactor authentication. Smart account lockout mitigates credential attacks by locking accounts after repeated failed sign-in attempts, helping defend against brute-force and password-spray attempts.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft 365 tenant that includes two groups named Group1 and Group2.  
  
You use Microsoft Defender XDR to manage your company’s customers’ tenants.  
  
You need to ensure that users in Group1 can perform security tasks in every customer tenant. The solution must satisfy the following requirements:  
  
- Group1 users must be assigned only the Security Operator role in the customer tenants.  
- Group2 users must be able to assign the Security Operator role to Group1 users in the customer tenants.  
- The use of quest accounts must be minimized.  
- Administrative effort must be minimized.  
  
What should you include in the solution?

Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration provides cross-tenant authentication for Microsoft Defender XDR access. Customer tenants can grant the necessary, least-privileged Security Operator permissions to users who authenticate from the managing tenant, while groups can be used to simplify membership and role administration. Azure Lighthouse delegates access only to Azure subscriptions or resource groups through Azure built-in roles; it does not delegate Microsoft Entra Security Operator access for Defender XDR.

**Learn more:** [Set up Microsoft Defender multitenant management](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/unified-secops/mto-requirements) · [Onboard a customer to Azure Lighthouse](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/lighthouse/how-to/onboard-customer)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Entra B2B collaboration provides cross-tenant authentication for Microsoft Defender XDR access. Customer tenants can grant the necessary, least-privileged Security Operator permissions to users who authenticate from the managing tenant, while groups can be used to simplify membership and role administration. Azure Lighthouse delegates access only to Azure subscriptions or resource groups through Azure built-in roles; it does not delegate Microsoft Entra Security Operator access for Defender XDR.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription containing multiple apps, managed by continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines in Azure DevOps.  
  
You need to recommend DevSecOps controls for the **Commit the code** and **Build and test** CI/CD stages, based on the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure.  
  
Which testing method should you recommend for each stage?
definition.explanation:
SAST analyzes source code without running the application, allowing vulnerabilities to be identified as code is committed. DAST tests a running application from the outside, so it is performed after the application has been built and is available for testing. Cloud Adoption Framework guidance recommends integrating static code analysis early in CI/CD pipelines.

**Learn more:** [DevOps security considerations overview — Cloud Adoption Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/considerations/security-considerations-overview)

finalExplanation: SAST analyzes source code without running the application, allowing vulnerabilities to be identified as code is committed. DAST tests a running application from the outside, so it is performed after the application has been built and is available for testing. Cloud Adoption Framework guidance recommends integrating static code analysis early in CI/CD pipelines.

You need to recommend a solution that identifies and remediates virtual machines with these characteristics:  
  
- Are **not** onboarded to Defender for Servers

What should you include in the recommendation?
