definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You have a DNS domain named `contoso.com` hosted by a third-party DNS registrar.  
  
Developers use Azure DevOps to deploy web apps to App Service Environments. Whenever a new app is deployed, a CNAME record for that app is registered in `contoso.com`.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that secures the DNS record for every web app. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Ensure that when an app is deleted, its CNAME record is also removed.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
definition.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for App Service detects dangling DNS entries when an App Service website is decommissioned but its custom-domain DNS entry remains at the registrar. This protection applies when the domain is managed by an external DNS registrar, and it identifies the CNAME condition that must be remediated to prevent subdomain takeover. DNS-record deletion itself must be performed through the registrar or deployment-lifecycle automation.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Defender for App Service – benefits and features](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/defender-for-app-service-introduction) · [Prevent dangling DNS entries and avoid subdomain takeover](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/fundamentals/subdomain-takeover)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Defender for App Service detects dangling DNS entries when an App Service website is decommissioned but its custom-domain DNS entry remains at the registrar. This protection applies when the domain is managed by an external DNS registrar, and it identifies the CNAME condition that must be remediated to prevent subdomain takeover. DNS-record deletion itself must be performed through the registrar or deployment-lifecycle automation.

definition.stemRaw:

The company is planning an application with the architecture shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783896794557-z8udkzym.png)  
  
You are designing a logging and auditing solution for the proposed architecture. The solution must meet these requirements:

What should be included in the solution?

Microsoft Sentinel uses the Azure Web Application Firewall data connector to integrate and analyze WAF logs. Defender for Servers is the Microsoft Defender for Cloud plan that protects virtual machines and generates security alerts for those workloads.

**Learn more:** [Using Microsoft Sentinel with Azure Web Application Firewall](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/waf-sentinel) · [Protect your Virtual Machines (VMs) with Microsoft Defender for Servers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/tutorial-protect-resources)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Sentinel uses the Azure Web Application Firewall data connector to integrate and analyze WAF logs. Defender for Servers is the Microsoft Defender for Cloud plan that protects virtual machines and generates security alerts for those workloads.

You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
Domain1 is synchronized with the tenant by using Microsoft Entra Connect.  
  
You need to monitor Domain1 for privilege-escalation attacks.  
  
What should you use?

Microsoft Defender for Identity detects, investigates, and responds to identity-based attacks across on-premises, cloud, and hybrid environments. It monitors Active Directory signals and can detect privilege escalation and suspicious role or group membership changes.

definition.stemRaw:

The company enters into a contract with the United States government.  
  
You need to assess the current subscription for compliance with NIST 800-53.  
  
What should you do first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From Defender for Cloud, review the Azure security baseline for audit report.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, create an access policy for cloud applications.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From Defender for Cloud, enable Defender for Cloud plans.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From Azure Policy, assign a built-in initiative that has a scope of the subscription.

definition.explanation:
NIST SP 800-53 regulatory compliance is implemented through an Azure Policy built-in initiative. Assigning that initiative to the subscription establishes the scope that Defender for Cloud evaluates and reports against for compliance.

**Learn more:** [Assign regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/assign-regulatory-compliance-standards) · [Details of the NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 4 Regulatory Compliance built-in initiative](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/samples/nist-sp-800-53-r4)

finalExplanation: NIST SP 800-53 regulatory compliance is implemented through an Azure Policy built-in initiative. Assigning that initiative to the subscription establishes the scope that Defender for Cloud evaluates and reports against for compliance.

definition.stemRaw:
You have three Microsoft Entra tenants named Tenant1, Tenant2, and Tenant3.  
  
You have three Azure subscriptions named Sub1, Sub2, and Sub3. Each tenant is associated with multiple Azure subscriptions.  
  
Each subscription has one Microsoft Sentinel workspace, as shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783886028916-oz9g6qs6.png)  
  
You need to recommend a solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- Ensure that users in Tenant1 can manage resources in Sub2 and Sub3 without switching subscriptions or signing in to another tenant.  
- Implement multiple-workspace view for Sentinel2 and Sentinel3.  
  
What should you use to delegate permissions, and which Microsoft Sentinel feature can users manage in multiple-workspace view?
definition.explanation:
Azure Lighthouse lets a managing tenant access and manage delegated Azure resources in other tenants without changing directories. Microsoft Sentinel multiple-workspace view provides centralized incident management across workspaces, including viewing and handling incidents from the selected workspaces.

**Learn more:** [Azure Lighthouse documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/lighthouse/) · [Work with Microsoft Sentinel incidents in many workspaces at once](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/multiple-workspace-view)

finalExplanation: Azure Lighthouse lets a managing tenant access and manage delegated Azure resources in other tenants without changing directories. Microsoft Sentinel multiple-workspace view provides centralized incident management across workspaces, including viewing and handling incidents from the selected workspaces.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription and an Azure subscription. Microsoft 365 Defender and Microsoft Defender for Cloud are enabled.  
  
The Azure subscription has 50 virtual machines. Each virtual machine runs different applications on Windows Server 2019.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that ensures only authorized applications can run on the virtual machines. If an unauthorized application tries to run or be installed, it must be automatically blocked until an administrator authorizes it.  
  
Which security control should you recommend?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azure AD Conditional Access App Control policies

choices.label: C
choices.text: app discovery anomaly detection policies in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps

choices.label: D
choices.text: adaptive application controls in Defender for Cloud

definition.explanation:
Adaptive application controls in Microsoft Defender for Cloud use machine learning to identify known-safe applications and generate application allowlists for virtual machines. The allowlist can mandate that only approved applications run, preventing unapproved software from executing until it is authorized.

**Learn more:** [Azure security baseline for Windows virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/baselines/virtual-machines-windows-virtual-machines-security-baseline) · [Protect virtual machines with Microsoft Defender for Servers](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/tutorial-protect-resources)

finalExplanation: Adaptive application controls in Microsoft Defender for Cloud use machine learning to identify known-safe applications and generate application allowlists for virtual machines. The allowlist can mandate that only approved applications run, preventing unapproved software from executing until it is authorized.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an on-premises network and a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You are designing a Zero Trust security strategy.  
  
Which two security controls should you incorporate into the Zero Trust solution? Each correct answer represents part of the solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct answer is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Always allow connections from the on-premises network.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Disable passwordless sign-in for sensitive accounts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Block sign-in attempts from unknown locations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Block sign-in attempts from noncompliant devices.

definition.explanation:
Zero Trust requires explicit authentication and authorization using all available signals, including location and device health. Conditional access that blocks sign-ins from unknown locations and noncompliant devices enforces those signals; automatically trusting the on-premises network conflicts with Zero Trust, and passwordless sign-in is a security-strengthening authentication approach.

**Learn more:** [What is Zero Trust?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/zero-trust-overview) · [Zero Trust identity and device access configurations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-gb/security/zero-trust/zero-trust-identity-device-access-policies-overview)

finalExplanation: Zero Trust requires explicit authentication and authorization using all available signals, including location and device health. Conditional access that blocks sign-ins from unknown locations and noncompliant devices enforces those signals; automatically trusting the on-premises network conflicts with Zero Trust, and passwordless sign-in is a security-strengthening authentication approach.

definition.stemRaw:
You need to recommend a solution for scanning the application code. The solution must satisfy the application development requirements.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
definition.explanation:
GitHub Advanced Security includes code scanning, which analyzes repository code for potential security vulnerabilities and coding errors using CodeQL or supported third-party tools.

finalExplanation: GitHub Advanced Security includes code scanning, which analyzes repository code for potential security vulnerabilities and coding errors using CodeQL or supported third-party tools.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription containing three Azure App Service web apps.  
  
You need to protect the apps by using Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Azure Front Door. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Block attempts by malicious bots to access the apps.  
- Rate-limit incoming connections to the apps.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you configure for each requirement?
definition.explanation:
Azure Front Door WAF rate limiting is implemented with custom rate-limit rules. The managed Bot Manager rule set identifies and protects against bad bots, and Microsoft maintains the rule set, minimizing administrative effort.

**Learn more:** [What is rate limiting for Azure Front Door?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/afds/waf-front-door-rate-limit) · [Web Application Firewall DRS rule groups and rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/afds/waf-front-door-drs)

finalExplanation: Azure Front Door WAF rate limiting is implemented with custom rate-limit rules. The managed Bot Manager rule set identifies and protects against bad bots, and Microsoft maintains the rule set, minimizing administrative effort.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company has devices running Windows 10, Windows 11, or Windows Server.  
  
You are working to improve the devices' security posture.  
  
You plan to use security baselines from the Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit.  
  
What should you recommend to compare the baselines with the devices' current configurations?
definition.explanation:
Policy Analyzer is the Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit utility for analyzing and comparing Group Policy Objects. It can compare GPOs with current local policy and local registry settings, which enables assessment of a security baseline against an existing device configuration.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit Guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/operating-system-security/device-management/windows-security-configuration-framework/security-compliance-toolkit-10)

finalExplanation: Policy Analyzer is the Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit utility for analyzing and comparing Group Policy Objects. It can compare GPOs with current local policy and local registry settings, which enables assessment of a security baseline against an existing device configuration.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
You also have subscriptions for Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI).  
  
You create a custom security standard in Defender for Cloud.  
  
To which subscriptions can the Defender for Cloud standard be applied?

Microsoft Defender for Cloud custom security standards can be assigned to Azure subscriptions, AWS accounts, and GCP projects. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is not supported as a target scope for custom standards.

**Learn more:** [Create custom security standards and recommendations in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/create-custom-recommendations) · [Assign regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/assign-regulatory-compliance-standards)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud custom security standards can be assigned to Azure subscriptions, AWS accounts, and GCP projects. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure is not supported as a target scope for custom standards.

definition.stemRaw:
You are developing an application lifecycle management process based on the Microsoft Security Development Lifecycle (SDL).  
  
You need to recommend a security standard for onboarding applications to Azure. The standard will contain recommendations for application design, development, and deployment.  
  
What should be included during the application design phase?

choices.label: A
choices.text: software decomposition by using Microsoft Visual Studio Enterprise

choices.label: B
choices.text: dynamic application security testing (DAST) by using Veracode

choices.label: C
choices.text: threat modeling by using the Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool

choices.label: D

Microsoft SDL requires threat modeling during the design phase to identify, categorize, assess, and mitigate security threats before they become embedded in the application architecture. The Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool supports this SDL design-analysis activity.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Security Development Lifecycle (SDL)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/compliance/assurance/assurance-microsoft-security-development-lifecycle) · [Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/security/develop/threat-modeling-tool)

finalExplanation: Microsoft SDL requires threat modeling during the design phase to identify, categorize, assess, and mitigate security threats before they become embedded in the application architecture. The Microsoft Threat Modeling Tool supports this SDL design-analysis activity.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company has the virtual-machine infrastructure shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783810115742-sdr7pjb0.jpg)  
  
The company intends to use Microsoft Azure Backup Server (MABS) to back up the virtual machines to Azure.  
  
You need to recommend ways to increase backup-strategy resiliency and mitigate attacks such as ransomware.  
  
What should the recommendation include?

choices.label: C

finalExplanation: MABS uses a security PIN as an additional authentication layer for critical operations such as stopping protection and deleting backup data. Requiring the PIN helps prevent unauthorized disabling or deletion of backups during a ransomware attack.

definition.stemRaw:

During which phase of a CI/CD DevOps process should each security-related task take place?
definition.explanation:
Threat modeling identifies design risks and mitigations before implementation, so it belongs in planning and development. DAST tests a running application for vulnerabilities as part of building and testing. Actionable intelligence—such as monitoring, threat detection, and operational response—belongs in the operate phase.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark v2 - DevOps Security](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/benchmark/azure/mcsb-v2-devop-security) · [DevOps security considerations overview - Cloud Adoption Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/considerations/security-considerations-overview)

finalExplanation: Threat modeling identifies design risks and mitigations before implementation, so it belongs in planning and development. DAST tests a running application for vulnerabilities as part of building and testing. Actionable intelligence—such as monitoring, threat detection, and operational response—belongs in the operate phase.

definition.stemRaw:
You have two on-premises Windows Server servers named Server1 and Server2. Server1 hosts an app named App1 and is isolated from the internet.  
  
You have a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You plan to deploy Global Secure Access to provide remote access to App1.  
  
You need to configure the tenant and Server2 for the planned deployment. The solution must require users who try to access App1 to authenticate with their Microsoft Entra credentials.  
  
What should you create in the tenant, and what should you install on Server2?
definition.explanation:
A Global Secure Access enterprise application provides the container for private resources, user and group assignment, and Conditional Access. The Microsoft Entra private network connector runs on a Windows Server with access to the internal application and brokers its connection to Global Secure Access.

**Learn more:** [Learn about Microsoft Entra Private Access - Global Secure Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/concept-private-access) · [How to configure connectors for Microsoft Entra Private Access and application proxy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-configure-connectors)

definition.explanation:
Azure Arc connects on-premises and multicloud servers to Azure so they can be managed and governed as Azure resources. You are designing an Azure DevOps solution that deploys applications to an Azure subscription by using continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) pipelines.

The Azure subscription includes 50 virtual machines. Every virtual machine runs different applications on Windows Server 2019.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that ensures only authorized applications can run on the virtual machines. If an unauthorized application tries to run or be installed, it must be blocked automatically until an administrator authorizes the application.  
  
Which security control should you recommend?

choices.text: app registrations in the Microsoft Entra tenant

choices.label: B

choices.label: C

You are updating the deployment process to align it with the DevSecOps controls guidance in the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that ensures all code changes are submitted by using pull requests before the CI/CD workflow deploys them.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
definition.explanation:
Azure Repos branch policies can protect the deployment branch by requiring pull requests for all changes and rejecting direct pushes. This enforces the pull-request workflow before changes can reach the branch used by CI/CD deployments.

finalExplanation: Azure Repos branch policies can protect the deployment branch by requiring pull requests for all changes and rejecting direct pushes. This enforces the pull-request workflow before changes can reach the branch used by CI/CD deployments.

definition.stemRaw:
You have four Azure subscriptions named Sub1, Sub2, Sub3, and Sub4. Each subscription has a unique Microsoft Entra tenant linked to a Microsoft 365 subscription. Sub1 includes a user named User1.  
  
You plan to implement Microsoft Sentinel.  
  
You need User1 to monitor Microsoft Entra ID events and Microsoft 365 events for Sub2, Sub3, and Sub4 by using Microsoft Sentinel. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
What is the minimum number of Microsoft Sentinel workspaces you should create, and which Azure service should you use?
definition.explanation:
Microsoft Sentinel supports collection of Microsoft and Azure SaaS data only within the same Microsoft Entra tenant boundary. Each of the three source tenants therefore requires its own Sentinel-enabled Log Analytics workspace for Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365 data. Azure Lighthouse enables delegated management of Sentinel workspaces across tenants, allowing centralized monitoring with minimal administrative overhead.

**Learn more:** [Prepare for multiple workspaces and tenants in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/prepare-multiple-workspaces) · [Extend Microsoft Sentinel across workspaces and tenants](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/extend-sentinel-across-workspaces-tenants)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Sentinel supports collection of Microsoft and Azure SaaS data only within the same Microsoft Entra tenant boundary. Each of the three source tenants therefore requires its own Sentinel-enabled Log Analytics workspace for Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365 data. Azure Lighthouse enables delegated management of Sentinel workspaces across tenants, allowing centralized monitoring with minimal administrative overhead.

definition.stemRaw:

You have an Azure subscription named Sub2 that is connected to a Microsoft Entra tenant named fabrikam.com. Sub2 contains 20 virtual networks named Sub2_VNet1 through Sub2_VNet20.  
  
You need to deploy an Azure Virtual Network Manager solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- Blocks SSH traffic on Sub1_VNet20 and Sub2_VNet20 by using network security groups (NSGs)  
- Blocks SSH traffic on Sub1_VNet1 through Sub1_VNet19 and Sub2_VNet1 through Sub2_VNet19  
- Allows SSH traffic on Sub1_VNet20 and Sub2_VNet20  
- Blocks FTP traffic on all the virtual networks  
- Minimizes administrative effort  
  
What is the minimum number of components required for the deployment?

choices.label: A
choices.text: • 1 Virtual Network Manager instance• 1 rule collection• 2 NSGs

choices.label: B
choices.text: • 2 Virtual Network Manager instances that each contains:o 1 NSGo 1 rule collection

choices.label: C
choices.text: • 2 Virtual Network Manager instances that each contains:o 2 NSGso 2 rule collections

choices.label: D
choices.text: • 1 Virtual Network Manager instance• 2 rule collections• 2 NSGs

finalExplanation: Azure Virtual Network Manager supports cross-tenant connections, allowing one network manager to manage virtual networks in both tenants. definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to implement enterprise-scale landing zones based on the Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure. The deployment will include one platform landing zone for all shared services and three application landing zones, each of which will host a different Azure application.  
  
You need to recommend which resource to deploy to each landing zone. The solution must meet the Cloud Adoption Framework best-practice recommendations for enterprise-scale landing zones.  
  
What should you recommend?
definition.explanation:
Application landing zones host the resources for a single workload or application. Deploying an Azure Key Vault with each application landing zone keeps that workload’s keys, secrets, and certificates isolated within its own lifecycle and security boundary. Azure Firewall, virtual network gateways, and shared DNS are typically centralized platform connectivity services rather than duplicated for each application workload.

**Learn more:** [What is an Azure landing zone?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/landing-zone/) · [Deploy Azure landing zones](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/landing-zones/landing-zone-deploy)

finalExplanation: Application landing zones host the resources for a single workload or application. Deploying an Azure Key Vault with each application landing zone keeps that workload’s keys, secrets, and certificates isolated within its own lifecycle and security boundary. Azure Firewall, virtual network gateways, and shared DNS are typically centralized platform connectivity services rather than duplicated for each application workload.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company operates a hybrid cloud infrastructure.  
  
The company intends to hire several temporary employees over a short time. These employees must access applications and data on the company’s on-premises network.  
  
The company’s security policy prohibits using personal devices to access company data and applications.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that gives the temporary employee access to company resources. The solution must scale on demand.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Deploy Azure Virtual Desktop, Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Conditional Access, and Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Redesign the VPN infrastructure by adopting a split tunnel configuration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deploy Microsoft Endpoint Manager and Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Conditional Access.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Migrate the on-premises applications to cloud-based applications.

definition.explanation:
Azure Virtual Desktop delivers centrally managed virtual desktops or applications, allowing temporary workers to access company resources through a controlled remote session instead of directly using personal devices for company data and applications. Pooled multi-session resources and autoscale support scaling capacity as demand changes. Azure AD Conditional Access and Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps provide the access and session-security controls needed for this remote-access model.

**Learn more:** [What is Azure Virtual Desktop?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/overview) · [Innovation and Azure Virtual Desktop environment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/scenarios/azure-virtual-desktop/innovate)

finalExplanation: Azure Virtual Desktop delivers centrally managed virtual desktops or applications, allowing temporary workers to access company resources through a controlled remote session instead of directly using personal devices for company data and applications. definition.stemRaw:
Your company operates on-premises datacenters in Seattle, Chicago, and New York City.  
  
You plan to migrate the on-premises workloads to the East US Azure region.  
  
You need to design a governance solution for the management group hierarchy. The solution must follow Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework for Azure principles and ensure that the hierarchy aligns with the Azure landing conceptual architecture.  
  
What should you use to determine which archetype-aligned management groups to create under the landing zones management group?
definition.explanation:
In the Azure landing zones conceptual architecture, the principal workload archetypes are determined by connectivity requirements. The Corp management group is for workloads that need connectivity or hybrid connectivity to the corporate network, while Online is for workloads that need direct internet connectivity or no virtual network. These connectivity needs therefore determine the archetype-aligned management groups beneath Landing zones.

**Learn more:** [Management groups - Cloud Adoption Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cloud-adoption-framework/ready/landing-zone/design-area/resource-org-management-groups)

finalExplanation: In the Azure landing zones conceptual architecture, the principal workload archetypes are determined by connectivity requirements. The Corp management group is for workloads that need connectivity or hybrid connectivity to the corporate network, while Online is for workloads that need direct internet connectivity or no virtual network. These connectivity needs therefore determine the archetype-aligned management groups beneath Landing zones.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription containing App Service apps in four Azure regions, which users access from the internet.  
  
You plan to block requests to the apps when those requests contain security threats specified by the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) Core Rule Set (CRS).  
  
Design a solution that blocks the requests and meets these requirements:  
  
- Maintain access to the apps during a regional outage.  
- Minimize the number of required resources.  
  
What should the design include?
definition.explanation:
Azure Front Door provides a global entry point and can route traffic to App Service origins in multiple regions, enabling continued service when an origin region is unavailable. Enabling Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Front Door applies managed OWASP Core Rule Set protections and can block malicious web requests. This uses one global Front Door/WAF deployment instead of regional Application Gateway resources.

**Learn more:** [Azure Web Application Firewall on Azure Front Door overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/afds/afds-overview) · [Azure Front Door health probes and load balancing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/health-probes)

finalExplanation: Azure Front Door provides a global entry point and can route traffic to App Service origins in multiple regions, enabling continued service when an origin region is unavailable. Enabling Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Front Door applies managed OWASP Core Rule Set protections and can block malicious web requests. This uses one global Front Door/WAF deployment instead of regional Application Gateway resources.

definition.stemRaw:

You plan to deploy Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters that will host web services.  
  
You need to recommend an ingress controller solution to protect the hosted web services.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
definition.explanation:
Azure Application Gateway integrates with AKS through the Application Gateway Ingress Controller (AGIC) and provides layer 7 ingress. Application Gateway can also use Web Application Firewall (WAF) functionality and TLS policies to protect AKS-hosted web services from common web attacks.

**Learn more:** [What is Application Gateway Ingress Controller?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/application-gateway/ingress-controller-overview)

finalExplanation: Azure Application Gateway integrates with AKS through the Application Gateway Ingress Controller (AGIC) and provides layer 7 ingress. Application Gateway can also use Web Application Firewall (WAF) functionality and TLS policies to protect AKS-hosted web services from common web attacks.

definition.stemRaw:

Your Azure subscription contains:  
  
- A Log Analytics workspace  
- A Microsoft Defender Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) plan  
  
You need to deploy Update Management for the servers. What should you configure?
definition.explanation:
Classic Azure Automation Update Management is enabled through an Azure Automation account connected to a Log Analytics workspace. On-premises Windows and Linux servers use the Log Analytics agent for update assessment and deployment. The Azure Connected Machine agent is for Azure Arc onboarding, and Azure Monitor Agent is not the required agent for this classic solution.

**Learn more:** [Migrate to Azure Monitor Agent from Log Analytics agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/agents/azure-monitor-agent-migration)

On-premises Windows and Linux servers use the Log Analytics agent for update assessment and deployment. The Azure Connected Machine agent is for Azure Arc onboarding, and Azure Monitor Agent is not the required agent for this classic solution.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription that contains 20 App Service web apps providing services to external customers. Every web app has a unique certificate and key.  
  
Recommend a solution to manage the web apps' keys and certificates. The solution must:  
  
- Provide a single tenancy for key and certificate storage.  
- Maintain FIPS 140-2 Level 3 compliance.  
- Follow the principle of least privilege.  
- Minimize costs.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should be included in the recommendation?

blanks.label: Authorization mechanism:
blanks.answer: A single vault with role-based access control (RBAC) authorization
options: 20 vaults with role-based access control (RBAC) authorization
A single vault with role-based access control (RBAC) authorization
A single vault with role-based access control (RBAC) authorization and access policy-based authorization

definition.explanation:
Azure Key Vault Managed HSM offers a single-tenant HSM solution that meets FIPS 140-2 Level 3 requirements. A single instance minimizes the number of resources to administer, and Azure RBAC supports narrowly scoped role assignments to enforce least privilege. Key Vault RBAC and access policies are alternative data-plane authorization models; RBAC is the recommended model.

**Learn more:** [Azure Key Vault managed HSM overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/managed-hsm/overview) · [Azure RBAC vs. access policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/key-vault/general/rbac-access-policy)

finalExplanation: Azure Key Vault Managed HSM offers a single-tenant HSM solution that meets FIPS 140-2 Level 3 requirements. A single instance minimizes the number of resources to administer, and Azure RBAC supports narrowly scoped role assignments to enforce least privilege. Key Vault RBAC and access policies are alternative data-plane authorization models; RBAC is the recommended model.

definition.stemRaw:

You must recommend a security solution to monitor the following activities:  
  
- User accounts that might have been compromised  
- Users performing bulk file downloads from Microsoft SharePoint Online  
  
What should be included in the recommendation for each activity? Components may be used once, more than once, or not at all.

items: Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Conditional Access

definition.stemRaw:

You have an Azure subscription containing Azure App Service web apps. The apps have these characteristics:  
  
- The apps use third-party and open-source components.  
- The apps were developed using C#, Python, and Java.  
- The app deployment process is managed by using Azure DevOps.  
- The app source code is stored in GitHub Enterprise Cloud repositories and is protected by using GitHub Advanced Security.  
  
You need to reduce the risk of supply-chain attacks throughout the application lifecycle.  
  
What should you implement?

choices.label: C
choices.text: app governance in Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps

Dependabot alerts identify dependencies with known vulnerabilities by comparing a repository’s dependency graph with security advisories. This helps teams remediate vulnerable third-party and open-source components across supported ecosystems before attackers can exploit them.

**Learn more:** [Dependabot alerts](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/dependabot-alerts) · [Supply chain security](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/supply-chain-security)

definition.stemRaw:
You have 50 Azure subscriptions.  
  
You need to monitor resources in the subscriptions for compliance with the ISO 27001:2013 standards. The solution must minimize the effort needed to modify the list of policy definitions monitored for the subscriptions.  
  
What are two ways to accomplish this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct selection is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assign an initiative to a management group.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Assign a policy to each subscription.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Assign a policy to a management group.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Assign an initiative to each subscription.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Assign a blueprint to each subscription.

choices.label: F
choices.text: Assign a blueprint to a management group.

definition.explanation:
Azure Policy initiatives group related policy definitions into one managed compliance set. Definitions added to an assigned initiative become part of its existing assignments automatically. An initiative may be assigned at a management-group scope, which applies to child subscriptions, or assigned directly to subscriptions. Both approaches therefore allow the ISO 27001:2013 policy set to be changed centrally without revising a separate policy assignment for every definition. Azure Blueprints instead require assignments to be updated to use a newer published version.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Azure Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/overview) · [Azure Policy initiative definition structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/initiative-definition-structure)

finalExplanation: Azure Policy initiatives group related policy definitions into one managed compliance set. Definitions added to an assigned initiative become part of its existing assignments automatically. An initiative may be assigned at a management-group scope, which applies to child subscriptions, or assigned directly to subscriptions. Both approaches therefore allow the ISO 27001:2013 policy set to be changed centrally without revising a separate policy assignment for every definition. Azure Blueprints instead require assignments to be updated to use a newer published version.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription.

You need to recommend a password-storage solution for App1 that satisfies these requirements:

Your on-premises datacenter contains 100 servers. The servers run Windows Server and are backed up by using Microsoft Azure Backup Server (MABS).

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You plan to deploy Azure App Service apps by using Azure DevOps.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that ensures deployed apps remain compliant with Microsoft cloud security benchmark (MCSB) recommendations.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: DevOps security in Microsoft Defender for Cloud

choices.label: D
choices.text: a branch policy in Azure DevOps

definition.explanation:
The Microsoft cloud security benchmark is applied through Defender for Cloud as security recommendations that are backed by Azure Policy, and Azure Policy (using audit, deny, and DeployIfNotExists/Enforce effects) is what keeps deployed App Service resources compliant with MCSB recommendations — regardless of whether they were deployed via Azure DevOps. "DevOps security in Microsoft Defender for Cloud" (A) assesses pipeline/repository posture such as secret and IaC scanning, and Microsoft Defender for App Service (B) provides runtime threat protection; neither enforces resource-level MCSB compliance. A branch policy (D) governs source control, not Azure resource compliance. So Azure Policy is the recommendation.

**Learn more:** [Manage MCSB in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/manage-mcsb)

finalExplanation: The Microsoft cloud security benchmark is applied through Defender for Cloud as security recommendations that are backed by Azure Policy, and Azure Policy (using audit, deny, and DeployIfNotExists/Enforce effects) is what keeps deployed App Service resources compliant with MCSB recommendations — regardless of whether they were deployed via Azure DevOps. "DevOps security in Microsoft Defender for Cloud" (A) assesses pipeline/repository posture such as secret and IaC scanning, and Microsoft Defender for App Service (B) provides runtime threat protection; neither enforces resource-level MCSB compliance. A branch policy (D) governs source control, not Azure resource compliance. So Azure Policy is the recommendation.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company has two offices, named Office1 and Office2. The offices have 1,000 on-premises Windows 11 devices that are Microsoft Entra joined.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription and use Microsoft Intune.  
  
You plan to deploy Microsoft Entra Internet Access from the offices to Microsoft 365.  
  
You enable the Microsoft 365 profile and configure the following:  
  
- A traffic policy for all Microsoft 365 traffic  
- A linked Conditional Access policy configured as follows:  
  - Applies to all users  
  - Performs compliant-network checks  
  - Permits Microsoft 365 traffic from compliant devices  
- An assignment to all devices  
- An assignment to the remote network associated with Office1  
  
You deploy the Global Secure Access client to every device in Office2 and establish connections.  
  
Identify which users can access Microsoft 365 services from compliant devices and which users are blocked from accessing Microsoft 365 services when they use noncompliant devices.
definition.explanation:
A Microsoft traffic profile can forward traffic through either the Global Secure Access client or an assigned remote network. The compliant-network Conditional Access check is satisfied by users connected through the Global Secure Access service, including users behind the configured Office1 remote network. Thus, client-connected compliant devices in Office2 and devices in Office1 can access Microsoft 365. A noncompliant device in Office2 is not behind an assigned remote network and cannot satisfy the compliant-network check, whereas a device in Office1 can do so through the remote network.

**Learn more:** [Enable compliant network check with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-compliant-network) · [How to enable and manage the Microsoft profile](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-manage-microsoft-profile)

finalExplanation: A Microsoft traffic profile can forward traffic through either the Global Secure Access client or an assigned remote network. The compliant-network Conditional Access check is satisfied by users connected through the Global Secure Access service, including users behind the configured Office1 remote network. Thus, client-connected compliant devices in Office2 and devices in Office1 can access Microsoft 365. A noncompliant device in Office2 is not behind an assigned remote network and cannot satisfy the compliant-network check, whereas a device in Office1 can do so through the remote network.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You have a Conditional Access policy configured with these settings:  
  
- **Name:** Policy 1  
- **Assignments**  
  - **Users:**  
    - **Include:** All users  
  - **Target resources:**  
    - **Include:** Select apps; Office 365  
  - **Network:**  
    - **Include:** Any network or location  
    - **Exclude:** Selected networks and locations; Site1  
  - **Access controls:**  
    - **Grant:** Require multifactor authentication, Require Hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device  
  
You plan to implement the Zero Trust Rapid Modernization Plan (RaMP).  
  
You need to make sure that Policy1 aligns with RaMP best-practice recommendations.  
  
Which setting should you change?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Exclude: Selected networks and locations; Site1

choices.label: C
choices.text: Grant Require Hybrid Microsoft Entra joined device

definition.explanation:
RaMP calls for explicit validation of user and device trust before access on both public and private networks. An exclusion for Site1 prevents the Conditional Access requirements from being evaluated for connections from that location, creating implicit trust based on network location. The Site1 exclusion should be removed or changed so the controls apply there as well.

**Learn more:** [RaMP Checklist—Explicitly validate trust for all access requests](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/zero-trust/user-access-productivity-validate-trust) · [Conditional Access: Network assignment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-assignment-network)

finalExplanation: RaMP calls for explicit validation of user and device trust before access on both public and private networks. An exclusion for Site1 prevents the Conditional Access requirements from being evaluated for connections from that location, creating implicit trust based on network location. The Site1 exclusion should be removed or changed so the controls apply there as well.

You plan to deploy multiple virtual machines to host a custom app named App1. App1 will use secrets stored in Vault1, and the virtual machines will be redeployed regularly according to App1 usage demands.  
  
Recommend a solution that enables App1 to access the secrets in Vault1 while meeting these requirements:  
  
- Minimize the number of security principals that can access Vault1.  
- Minimize sensitive-data storage on the virtual machines.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which endpoint type and identity type should App1 use?

blanks.label: Endpoint type:
options: Microsoft Identity Platform OAuth 2.0 access token

A user-assigned managed identity can be shared by multiple VMs and has an independent lifecycle, so one identity can be granted Key Vault access even as VMs are redeployed. Managed identities eliminate application-managed credentials. Code on an Azure VM requests the managed-identity token from the local Azure Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) endpoint.

**Learn more:** [How managed identities work with Azure virtual machines](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/how-managed-identities-work-vm) · [Use managed identities on a virtual machine to acquire an access token](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/how-to-use-vm-token)

definition.stemRaw:
Your company wants to optimize investigations of ransomware incidents.  
  
You need to recommend a ransomware-incident investigation plan based on the Microsoft Detection and Response Team (DART) approach.  
  
Which three actions should the plan perform in sequence?

slots.answer: Assess the current situation and identify the scope.
Identify which line-of-business (LOB) apps are unavailable due to a ransomware incident.

items: Identify which line-of-business (LOB) apps are unavailable due to a ransomware incident.
Implement a comprehensive strategy to reduce the risk of privileged access compromise.
Assess the current situation and identify the scope.
Update organizational processes to manage major ransomware events and streamline outsourcing to avoid friction.
definition.explanation:
Microsoft Incident Response’s DART ransomware approach first assesses the current situation to understand the scope. Next, it identifies the affected line-of-business applications so systems can be brought back online. Finally, it determines the compromise recovery process to remove the threat actor from the environment. Privileged-access hardening and organizational-process updates are broader resilience measures rather than these three investigation steps.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Incident Response ransomware approach and best practices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/ransomware/incident-response-playbook-dart-ransomware-approach)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Incident Response’s DART ransomware approach first assesses the current situation to understand the scope. Next, it identifies the affected line-of-business applications so systems can be brought back online. Finally, it determines the compromise recovery process to remove the threat actor from the environment. Privileged-access hardening and organizational-process updates are broader resilience measures rather than these three investigation steps.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription containing a resource group named RG1. RG1 includes multiple Azure Files shares.  
  
You need to recommend a backup solution for the shares that meets these requirements:  
  
- Prevent deletion of backups and of the vault that stores them.  
- Prevent privilege-escalation attacks against the backup solution.  
- Prevent changes to the backup retention period.  
  
Which three actions should be performed, in sequence?
items: From RG1, create a resource lock.
definition.explanation:
Azure Files backup uses a Recovery Services vault. Enabling vault immutability blocks backup-loss operations and retention reductions; locking it makes the setting irreversible and protects against malicious privileged actors disabling immutability to delete or modify backups. A resource lock on RG1 is not a substitute for immutable-vault protection.

**Learn more:** [Azure Backup immutable vault overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-immutable-vault-concept) · [Manage Azure Backup immutable vault operations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-immutable-vault-how-to-manage)

finalExplanation: Azure Files backup uses a Recovery Services vault. Enabling vault immutability blocks backup-loss operations and retention reductions; locking it makes the setting irreversible and protects against malicious privileged actors disabling immutability to delete or modify backups. A resource lock on RG1 is not a substitute for immutable-vault protection.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a multicloud environment containing an Azure subscription and an Amazon Web Services (AWS) subscription.  
  
You need to design a solution that meets these requirements:  
  
- Dynamically discover the permissions granted to and used by each user.  
- Generate an aggregated metric that evaluates the risk level associated with unused or excessive permissions.  
- Automatically revoke permissions unused for 90 days.  
- Support granting on-demand permissions for limited periods.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which cloud service should you use for each subscription?

blanks.label: Azure:
options: Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in Microsoft Entra ID

blanks.label: AWS:
options: Privileged Identity Management (PIM) in Microsoft Entra ID

finalExplanation: Microsoft Entra Permissions Management is a CIEM solution that provides unified visibility across Azure, AWS, and GCP, so a single service covers both subscriptions and minimizes administrative effort. It discovers the permissions granted to and actually used by each identity, produces the Permission Creep Index (an aggregated metric of risk from unused or excessive permissions), can automatically delete permissions unused for 90 days, and offers permissions-on-demand for time-limited elevation. Privileged Identity Management (PIM) is Azure/Entra-only and, although it grants just-in-time roles, it does not discover used permissions, does not compute a permissions-risk metric, and cannot auto-revoke 90-day-unused permissions, so it fails the requirements for the Azure blank. Defender for Cloud (posture/workload security) and Entra External ID (B2B/B2C identity) address none of these entitlement-management needs.

choices.label: C

You plan to manage access to App1 for Los Angeles office users by using Microsoft Entra Private Access. You will deploy Private Access by taking these actions:  
  
- Provision an ExpressRoute circuit from the New York City office to the nearest peering location.  
- Create an Azure virtual network named VNet1 in the East US Azure region.  
- Deploy a Microsoft Entra application proxy connector to VNet1.  
  
You need to optimize the network for this planned deployment. The solution must:  
  
- Maximize redundancy for connectivity to App1.  
- Minimize network latency when accessing App1.  
- Minimize complexity.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
What should the solution include?

blanks.label: To optimize the connection between the users and the application proxy, deploy:

options: A connector to the default connector group and a connector to a new connector group
Two connectors to the default connector group
Two new connector groups that each contain a new connector

Azure private peering connects the on-premises network to resources in an Azure virtual network, so it provides the needed private path between VNet1’s connector and App1. ExpressRoute Premium is only needed for cross-geopolitical-region connectivity and is not required here.

ExpressRoute Premium is only needed for cross-geopolitical-region connectivity and is not required here.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an on-premises server running Windows Server that hosts a Microsoft SQL Server database named DB1.  
  
You plan to migrate DB1 to Azure.  
  
You need to recommend an encrypted Azure database solution that satisfies these requirements:  
  
- Minimizes the risk of malware using elevated privileges to access sensitive data  
- Prevents database administrators from accessing sensitive data  
- Enables pattern matching for server-side database operations  
- Supports Microsoft Azure Attestation  
- Uses hardware-based encryption  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines with virtualization-based security (VBS) enclaves

choices.label: B
choices.text: Azure SQL Database with virtualization-based security (VBS) enclaves

choices.label: C
choices.text: Azure SQL Managed Instance that has Always Encrypted configured

choices.label: D
choices.text: Azure SQL Database with Intel Software Guard Extensions (Intel SGX) enclaves

definition.explanation:
Azure SQL Database with Intel SGX enclaves supports Always Encrypted with secure enclaves, allowing richer confidential queries such as pattern matching while keeping plaintext unavailable to database administrators who do not hold the encryption keys. Intel SGX is a hardware-based trusted execution environment, and Azure SQL Database uses Microsoft Azure Attestation for SGX enclave attestation. SGX with Azure Attestation provides stronger protection against attacks by actors with operating-system-level administrative access than VBS enclaves; VBS enclaves in Azure SQL Database do not support attestation.

**Learn more:** [Plan for secure enclaves in Azure SQL Database](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/always-encrypted-enclaves-plan?view=azuresql) · [Configure attestation for Always Encrypted using Azure Attestation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-sql/database/always-encrypted-enclaves-configure-attestation?view=azuresql)

finalExplanation: Azure SQL Database with Intel SGX enclaves supports Always Encrypted with secure enclaves, allowing richer confidential queries such as pattern matching while keeping plaintext unavailable to database administrators who do not hold the encryption keys. Intel SGX is a hardware-based trusted execution environment, and Azure SQL Database uses Microsoft Azure Attestation for SGX enclave attestation. SGX with Azure Attestation provides stronger protection against attacks by actors with operating-system-level administrative access than VBS enclaves; VBS enclaves in Azure SQL Database do not support attestation.

definition.stemRaw:
You are creating a ransomware-mitigation strategy.  
  
You conduct a ransomware risk assessment and identify business-critical assets.  
  
You need to recommend a solution for mitigating ransomware threats. The solution must align with Microsoft security best practices.  
  
Which two actions should you include in the recommendation? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.  
  
**NOTE:** Each correct answer is worth one point.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Enable firewall logging for auditing, without restricting inbound or outbound traffic.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use extended patching cycles to reduce the risk of update-related service disruptions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Implement immutable, offline backups that have restricted access and test restore procedures regularly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Deploy Privileged Identity Management (PIM) that uses just-in-time (JIT) access and approval workflows.

definition.explanation:
Immutable and offline backups with restricted access protect recovery data from ransomware-driven encryption or deletion; regularly testing restores verifies that critical systems can actually be recovered. Privileged Identity Management reduces the exposure of privileged accounts through just-in-time, time-bound access and approval-controlled activation, limiting the opportunity for attackers to misuse standing administrative privileges.

**Learn more:** [Prepare for ransomware attacks with a backup and recovery plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security/ransomware/protect-against-ransomware-phase1) · [Plan a Privileged Identity Management deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-governance/privileged-identity-management/pim-deployment-plan)

finalExplanation: Immutable and offline backups with restricted access protect recovery data from ransomware-driven encryption or deletion; regularly testing restores verifies that critical systems can actually be recovered. Privileged Identity Management reduces the exposure of privileged accounts through just-in-time, time-bound access and approval-controlled activation, limiting the opportunity for attackers to misuse standing administrative privileges.

What should the solution include for each requirement?

definition.explanation:

definition.stemRaw:
You are assessing an Azure environment for compliance.  
  
You need to design an Azure Policy implementation that can evaluate compliance without modifying any resources.  
  
Which Azure Policy effect should you use?
definition.explanation:
Azure Policy's Deny effect evaluates existing resources against the policy rule and marks non-compliant matches as non-compliant without changing any resource properties; it only prevents new or updated requests that don't match the standard from being created, returning a 403 rather than altering the resource. Modify and Append effects actively add or change resource properties/tags, and Disabled effect skips genuine evaluation (resources default to Compliant), so Deny is the effect that assesses compliance while leaving resources unmodified.

**Learn more:** [Azure Policy definitions deny effect - Azure Policy | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/effect-deny) · [Azure Policy definitions disabled effect - Azure Policy | Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/policy/concepts/effect-disabled)

Modify and Append effects actively add or change resource properties/tags, and Disabled effect skips genuine evaluation (resources default to Compliant), so Deny is the effect that assesses compliance while leaving resources unmodified.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: You recommend creating private endpoints for the web app and the database layer.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
definition.explanation:
An Azure App Service private endpoint secures inbound access to the app only; it is not used for outbound connections from the app. Private access from the web app to Azure Cosmos DB requires App Service virtual network integration, private DNS resolution, and a Cosmos DB private endpoint. Creating private endpoints alone therefore does not provide the required private database connection.

**Learn more:** [Use private endpoints for Azure App Service apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-private-endpoint) · [Integrate your app with an Azure virtual network](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/overview-vnet-integration)

finalExplanation: An Azure App Service private endpoint secures inbound access to the app only; it is not used for outbound connections from the app. Private access from the web app to Azure Cosmos DB requires App Service virtual network integration, private DNS resolution, and a Cosmos DB private endpoint. Creating private endpoints alone therefore does not provide the required private database connection.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: You recommend using Azure Key Vault to store the credentials.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure Key Vault protects Azure Cosmos DB credentials from being stored in application code or clear-text configuration. Azure App Service can retrieve Key Vault secrets by using a managed identity, restricting secret access to the workload and enabling secure credential use for the database connection.

**Learn more:** [Store and use Azure Cosmos DB credentials with Azure Key Vault](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/store-credentials-key-vault) · [Use Key Vault references as app settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/app-service/app-service-key-vault-references)

finalExplanation: Azure Key Vault protects Azure Cosmos DB credentials from being stored in application code or clear-text configuration. Azure App Service can retrieve Key Vault secrets by using a managed identity, restricting secret access to the workload and enabling secure credential use for the database connection.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: You recommend deploying Azure Application Gateway with Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF).  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure Application Gateway with WAF protects web applications against common HTTP-based exploits and vulnerabilities, primarily at the web application's ingress. It does not secure the Azure App Service-to-Azure Cosmos DB connection with private, explicitly authorized network access. Azure Cosmos DB can be restricted to private endpoints and have public network access disabled to support this Zero Trust requirement.

**Learn more:** [What is Azure Web Application Firewall on Azure Application Gateway?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/ag/ag-overview) · [Configure Azure Private Link for an Azure Cosmos DB account](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/how-to-configure-private-endpoints)

finalExplanation: Azure Application Gateway with WAF protects web applications against common HTTP-based exploits and vulnerabilities, primarily at the web application's ingress. It does not secure the Azure App Service-to-Azure Cosmos DB connection with private, explicitly authorized network access. Azure Cosmos DB can be restricted to private endpoints and have public network access disabled to support this Zero Trust requirement.

definition.stemRaw:
Solution: You recommend deploying Azure Front Door with Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF).  
  
Does this fulfill the goal?
definition.explanation:
Azure Front Door WAF protects incoming web application requests at the network edge from common web exploits; it is not a control for the application-to-Azure Cosmos DB connection. Securing that connection under Zero Trust requires private network access and explicit identity-based authorization for the workload.

**Learn more:** [Azure Web Application Firewall on Azure Front Door](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/web-application-firewall/afds/afds-overview) · [Secure your Azure Front Door deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/frontdoor/secure-front-door)

finalExplanation: Azure Front Door WAF protects incoming web application requests at the network edge from common web exploits; it is not a control for the application-to-Azure Cosmos DB connection. Securing that connection under Zero Trust requires private network access and explicit identity-based authorization for the workload.

definition.stemRaw:
Your network has an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain named Domain1. Domain1 has 10 domain controllers.  
  
You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that includes a Microsoft Sentinel workspace named WS1.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription with 5,000 users. Every user has a Microsoft 365 E3 license.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to ingest security logs from every domain controller into WS1. The solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- The cost of ingesting data into WS1 must be minimized.  
- WS1 must ingest all Windows Security event logs generated by the domain controllers.  
- The solution must support approximately 350 MB of logs generated daily by each domain controller.  
  
What should you recommend?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Upgrade the user licenses to Microsoft 365 E5.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Onboard each domain controller to Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 2.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Configure a volume cap for WS1.

choices.label: E

definition.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Servers Plan 2 includes 500 MB of free daily ingestion per protected node for eligible security data. Windows Security events sent through the Microsoft-SecurityEvent stream to the SecurityEvent table qualify. With 10 domain controllers, the combined allowance is 5 GB per day, which exceeds the approximately 3.5 GB per day generated by the controllers while allowing all their Windows Security events to be ingested.
