definition.stemRaw:
You have an on-premises datacenter and an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster called AKS1.  
  
You need to limit Internet access to AKS1’s public endpoint. The solution must ensure that AKS1 is accessible only from the public IP addresses associated with the on-premises datacenter.  
  
What should you use?
definition.explanation:
AKS API server authorized IP ranges provide an allowlist of public IP addresses or CIDR ranges that can reach the public control-plane endpoint. Configuring the on-premises datacenter’s public IP addresses restricts access to those addresses.

**Learn more:** [API Server Authorized IP Ranges in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/aks/api-server-authorized-ip-ranges)

finalExplanation: AKS API server authorized IP ranges provide an allowlist of public IP addresses or CIDR ranges that can reach the public control-plane endpoint. Configuring the on-premises datacenter’s public IP addresses restricts access to those addresses.

definition.stemRaw:
Your Microsoft Entra tenant contains 800 Microsoft Entra joined devices and 700 users. Each user is assigned a single device. All the devices are onboarded to Global Secure Access.  
  
You use a software as a service (SaaS) application named App1 that is hosted by a third party. Users access App1 over the internet.  
  
You need to ensure that all the devices access App1 through the Global Secure Access client.  
  
What should you use?

finalExplanation: Global Secure Access uses traffic forwarding profiles (Microsoft traffic, Private access, and Internet access) to determine which network traffic is routed through the Global Secure Access client. Because App1 is an internet-hosted SaaS application, you must enable and configure the Internet Access traffic forwarding profile so that traffic destined for App1 is tunneled through the Global Secure Access client rather than going directly to the internet. Conditional Access policies can require the Global Secure Access client or a compliant network as a sign-in condition, but they do not control which traffic is actually forwarded through the client; that forwarding behavior is governed by the traffic forwarding profile configuration.

definition.stemRaw:
Your organization has a Microsoft Entra tenant configured with Microsoft Entra Private Access.  
  
You are planning to publish a set of internal web applications using a Global Secure Access application.  
  
You need to make sure users can reach these web apps by connecting through the Global Secure Access application.  
  
What should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: a Conditional Access policy that grants access from only compliant devices

choices.label: B
choices.text: a forwarding profile that directs all outbound internet traffic through the Microsoft backbone network

choices.label: C
choices.text: a connector group that contains the connectors used to access the web apps and a single endpoint for the internal fully qualified domain names (FQDNs)

choices.label: D
choices.text: an access policy that limits connections based on user groups

finalExplanation: To publish internal resources through a Global Secure Access (Private Access) Enterprise application, you must configure a private network connector group containing the connectors that can reach the target resources, and then add an application segment that specifies the internal fully qualified domain name (or IP address/range) and port for the web app. This connector group and FQDN endpoint definition is what enables the Global Secure Access client to intercept traffic destined for that FQDN, route it through the service, and have the connector forward it to the internal web app. Without this configuration, there is no mapping between the published app and the internal resource, so no traffic can be routed even if access policies or Conditional Access controls are in place.

definition.stemRaw:
Your company has an Azure subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Cloud.  
  
The company has just signed a contract with the United States government.  
  
You need to review the current subscription for NIST 800-53 compliance.  
  
What should you do first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: From Azure Policy, assign a built-in policy definition that has a scope of the subscription.

choices.label: B
choices.text: From Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps, create an access policy for cloud applications.

choices.label: C
choices.text: From Microsoft Defender for Cloud, turn on a security standard.

choices.label: D
choices.text: From Microsoft Defender for Cloud, review the secure score recommendations.

definition.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud's Regulatory Compliance dashboard evaluates a subscription against industry, regulatory, and benchmark standards, but only against standards that have been assigned to that scope. NIST SP 800-53 is not enabled by default, so to review compliance you must first enable it: navigate to Defender for Cloud > Regulatory compliance > Manage compliance policies, select the subscription, open Security policies, and toggle the NIST SP 800-53 standard to On. Once enabled, Defender for Cloud maps its continuous assessments to the NIST 800-53 controls and displays compliant/non-compliant status in the Regulatory Compliance dashboard.

**Learn more:** [Regulatory compliance in Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/concept-regulatory-compliance-standards) · [Assign regulatory compliance standards in Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/update-regulatory-compliance-packages)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud's Regulatory Compliance dashboard evaluates a subscription against industry, regulatory, and benchmark standards, but only against standards that have been assigned to that scope. NIST SP 800-53 is not enabled by default, so to review compliance you must first enable it: navigate to Defender for Cloud > Regulatory compliance > Manage compliance policies, select the subscription, open Security policies, and toggle the NIST SP 800-53 standard to On. Once enabled, Defender for Cloud maps its continuous assessments to the NIST 800-53 controls and displays compliant/non-compliant status in the Regulatory Compliance dashboard.

definition.stemRaw:
Your network contains an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to evaluate the security and governance of the domains. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Identify configuration issues and administrative vulnerabilities.  
- Minimize effort.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

finalExplanation: Microsoft Defender for Identity includes identity security posture assessments that proactively scan on-premises Active Directory (via its existing sensors) for known misconfigurations, legacy/insecure protocol usage, risky Group Policy settings, and administrative account vulnerabilities. These assessments are surfaced automatically in Microsoft Secure Score with remediation guidance, requiring no extra setup effort beyond the already-deployed sensors — directly meeting the requirement to identify configuration issues and administrative vulnerabilities while minimizing effort. Microsoft Entra ID Protection addresses cloud sign-in/user risk rather than on-prem AD misconfigurations, Microsoft Defender for Servers targets server workload threat protection, and Microsoft Sentinel would require significant custom engineering to achieve equivalent identity governance insights.

definition.stemRaw:
You manage a Microsoft Entra tenant containing two users, User1 and User2.  
  
An audit found that User1 has been permanently assigned the User Administrator role, despite the account belonging to a former contractor.  
  
The security team requires that:  
  
- All privileged role assignments are periodically validated.  
- Privileged Identity Management (PIM) is used to automate and enforce this validation process.  
  
You need to configure User2 so that the security requirements can be met, while following the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should be assigned to User2, and which tool should User2 use?

finalExplanation: Privileged Role Administrator is the least-privileged built-in role that can manage Privileged Identity Management settings and administer role assignments for Microsoft Entra roles, including configuring PIM and access reviews for privileged roles — Global Administrator would grant far more rights than needed, and Security Administrator lacks rights to manage PIM role assignments. Access reviews, run within PIM, let administrators schedule recurring attestations so that reviewers (or self-review) confirm privileged role assignments, such as the User Administrator role held by a former contractor, are still required; unconfirmed or denied assignments can be automatically removed, satisfying the requirement for periodic validation enforced through PIM. Access packages and Lifecycle workflows address entitlement management and joiner/mover/leaver automation respectively, not recurring validation of existing privileged role assignments.

definition.stemRaw:
Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes a Microsoft SharePoint Online site named Site1. All users hold a Microsoft 365 E5 license.  
  
Microsoft Intune is used to manage corporate devices.  
  
You are planning to create a Conditional Access policy that will permit access to Site1 only from devices that have been onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You need to ensure that the devices can be evaluated for compliance by using Intune before the policy is enforced.  
  
What should you create first?

finalExplanation: Conditional Access policies that require device compliance rely on Intune compliance policies to evaluate whether a device meets specified criteria—such as being onboarded to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and having an acceptable machine risk score—before the device is marked compliant. Only after a compliance policy is created and devices are evaluated against it can a Conditional Access policy use the 'require device to be marked as compliant' grant control to enforce access restrictions to resources like a SharePoint Online site. Windows Autopilot deployment profiles handle device provisioning, not compliance evaluation; app protection and app configuration policies apply to mobile application management scenarios rather than device-level compliance tied to Defender for Endpoint risk signals.

definition.stemRaw:
Your network includes an on-premises Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain that is synchronized with a Microsoft Entra tenant.  
  
You need to evaluate the domain to identify potential credential exposure risks. Your solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Provide actionable recommendations to help mitigate the risks.  
- Minimize the amount of administrative effort required.  
  
What should you use?

finalExplanation: Microsoft Defender for Identity continuously monitors on-premises AD DS (and hybrid identity infrastructure) and generates identity security posture assessments, including detection of exposed or leaked credentials (such as plaintext passwords stored in AD attributes) and other identity-related misconfigurations. Each assessment provides prioritized, actionable remediation guidance, and because monitoring is automated and continuous once sensors are deployed, it satisfies the requirement to minimize administrative effort. Microsoft Secure Score aggregates recommendations across products but does not itself perform the deep AD credential exposure analysis; Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps targets cloud/SaaS app usage and shadow IT rather than on-prem AD; and the Microsoft Assessment and Planning (MAP) Toolkit is a legacy inventory tool for migration planning, not security risk assessment.

definition.stemRaw:
You have 500 on-premises Windows devices enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to ensure that all outbound HTTP and HTTPS traffic from the devices is inspected using Microsoft Entra Internet Access. The solution must minimize infrastructure and operational costs.  
  
What should you include in the solution?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Deploy Network Policy Server (NPS) as a RADIUS proxy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Deploy Network Policy Server (NPS) as a RADIUS server.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Onboard the Global Secure Access client to the devices.

definition.explanation:
Microsoft Entra Internet Access (part of Global Secure Access) inspects internet-bound HTTP/HTTPS traffic by having devices route that traffic through the Global Secure Access cloud service. This requires installing/onboarding the Global Secure Access client on the endpoints so traffic can be forwarded per the configured Microsoft traffic forwarding profile, without deploying any additional on-premises infrastructure such as proxy servers or RADIUS/NPS components. Private network connectors instead enable Microsoft Entra Private Access to reach on-premises private applications and are unrelated to inspecting general internet traffic.

**Learn more:** [What is Global Secure Access?](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/overview-what-is-global-secure-access) · [Deploy the Global Secure Access client for Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/global-secure-access/how-to-install-windows-client)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Entra Internet Access (part of Global Secure Access) inspects internet-bound HTTP/HTTPS traffic by having devices route that traffic through the Global Secure Access cloud service. This requires installing/onboarding the Global Secure Access client on the endpoints so traffic can be forwarded per the configured Microsoft traffic forwarding profile, without deploying any additional on-premises infrastructure such as proxy servers or RADIUS/NPS components. Private network connectors instead enable Microsoft Entra Private Access to reach on-premises private applications and are unrelated to inspecting general internet traffic.

definition.stemRaw:
Your Azure subscription contains 1,000 virtual machines.  
  
You are planning to enforce a corporate standard requiring that all virtual machines have just-in-time (JIT) VM access enabled.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that will identify which of the virtual machines support JIT VM access.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

finalExplanation: Just-in-time VM access is a capability of Microsoft Defender for Cloud (part of Defender for Servers). Defender for Cloud evaluates each VM against JIT eligibility requirements—such as having an associated Network Security Group and being deployed via Azure Resource Manager—and reports, through its recommendations and workload protection dashboard, which VMs are supported for JIT and which are not, letting an organization identify and remediate machines that don't yet meet the standard. Azure Bastion provides browser-based RDP/SSH connectivity but does not assess or report JIT eligibility; Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps is a cloud access security broker for SaaS applications; Microsoft Intune manages devices/endpoints and is unrelated to Azure VM network security posture.

definition.stemRaw:
You have 500 on-premises Windows devices that are joined to a Microsoft Entra tenant named Tenant1 and enrolled in Microsoft Intune.  
  
You have an Azure subscription named Sub1 that is linked to Tenant1.  
  
You have a partner company that has an Azure subscription named Sub2. Sub2 contains a virtual network named VNet2 and a storage account named storage1. storage1 is secured by using an Azure Private Link endpoint on VNet2.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that ensures all the users at your company can access storage1. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- The users must sign in from a compliant device before accessing storage1.  
- Access must NOT expose or provide connectivity to any other resources in Sub2.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation, and what should you recommend creating in Tenant1?

blanks.label: Create:
options: A Global Secure Access security profile
A Microsoft Entra application proxy connector

finalExplanation: Microsoft Entra Private Access (a Global Secure Access capability) is purpose-built to extend Zero Trust, VPN-less access to private resources such as an Azure Storage account secured behind an Azure Private Link private endpoint. You publish the resource by creating a Global Secure Access application (per-app / Enterprise application) with an application segment for the storage account's FQDN (e.g., storage1.blob.core.windows.net) on port 443, routed through a Microsoft Entra private network connector deployed with network reachability to the private endpoint. Microsoft's guidance explicitly states that traffic routed to an application segment is delivered to that internal resource 'without any ability to connect to other resources on your network,' which satisfies the requirement to avoid exposing other Sub2 resources — something a Site-to-Site VPN or VNet peering could not guarantee, since both grant broad, subnet-level network connectivity into VNet2. Microsoft Entra Internet Access is unsuitable because it is a Secure Web Gateway for internet/SaaS traffic, not for privately-linked PaaS resources on a partner's VNet. Once the Global Secure Access application is created, a Conditional Access policy is applied at the application level requiring the device to be marked as compliant (via Intune), enforcing that only compliant devices can sign in before reaching storage1. An access package only handles entitlement/assignment workflows, a Global Secure Access security profile only links Conditional Access to traffic-forwarding profiles rather than defining the per-resource segment, and an application proxy connector is scoped to publishing HTTP/HTTPS web apps rather than brokering Private Link-based storage access.

definition.stemRaw:
You manage a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes 1,000 Microsoft Exchange Online mailboxes.  
  
You need to determine which users are vulnerable to phishing attacks.  
  
What should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: spoof intelligence insight in Exchange Online Protection (EOP)

choices.label: B
choices.text: Attack path analysis in Microsoft Defender for Cloud

choices.label: C
choices.text: Attack simulation training in Microsoft Defender for Office 365

choices.label: D
choices.text: user activity reports in Microsoft Purview insider risk management

definition.explanation:
Attack simulation training, part of Microsoft Defender for Office 365, lets administrators launch realistic simulated phishing (and other social engineering) attacks against their organization's users. The results show which users clicked malicious links, opened attachments, or submitted credentials, directly identifying which users are susceptible to phishing. This is distinct from spoof intelligence (which analyzes spoofed senders), attack path analysis (which maps exploitable paths to cloud resources), and insider risk management activity reports (which track potentially risky internal behaviors like data leakage, not phishing susceptibility).

**Learn more:** [Get started using Attack simulation training in Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/security/office-365-security/attack-simulation-training-get-started)

finalExplanation: Attack simulation training, part of Microsoft Defender for Office 365, lets administrators launch realistic simulated phishing (and other social engineering) attacks against their organization's users. The results show which users clicked malicious links, opened attachments, or submitted credentials, directly identifying which users are susceptible to phishing. This is distinct from spoof intelligence (which analyzes spoofed senders), attack path analysis (which maps exploitable paths to cloud resources), and insider risk management activity reports (which track potentially risky internal behaviors like data leakage, not phishing susceptibility).

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription that includes virtual machines, storage accounts, and Azure SQL databases.  
  
All resources are backed up multiple times per day using Azure Backup.  
  
You are developing a strategy to protect against ransomware attacks.  
  
You need to recommend which control must be enabled so that Azure Backup can be used to restore the resources if a ransomware attack succeeds.  
  
Which control should you include in the recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Perform offline backups to Azure Data Box.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Use Azure Monitor notifications when backup configurations change.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Encrypt backups by using customer-managed keys (CMKs).

definition.explanation:
Azure Backup provides a security feature that requires an additional layer of authentication—a security PIN generated from the Azure portal—before critical operations can be performed, such as disabling soft delete, changing backup policies to reduce retention periods, or deleting backup items and recovery points. This control prevents an attacker (or a compromised account) who has gained control of the subscription during a ransomware attack from being able to delete or tamper with existing backups, thereby ensuring that clean, recoverable backup data remains available for restoration after the attack. This is part of Microsoft's documented ransomware protection guidance for Azure Backup ('Security features to help protect Azure Backup and recovery data from ransomware attacks').

**Learn more:** [Security features to help protect against ransomware attacks - Azure Backup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/backup/backup-azure-security-feature-cloud)

finalExplanation: Azure Backup provides a security feature that requires an additional layer of authentication—a security PIN generated from the Azure portal—before critical operations can be performed, such as disabling soft delete, changing backup policies to reduce retention periods, or deleting backup items and recovery points. This control prevents an attacker (or a compromised account) who has gained control of the subscription during a ransomware attack from being able to delete or tamper with existing backups, thereby ensuring that clean, recoverable backup data remains available for restoration after the attack. This is part of Microsoft's documented ransomware protection guidance for Azure Backup ('Security features to help protect Azure Backup and recovery data from ransomware attacks').

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to enforce ISO 27002:2022 standards for new resources deployed to the subscription. The solution must ensure that noncompliant resources are automatically detected.  
  
What should you use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the regulatory compliance dashboard in Microsoft Defender for Cloud

finalExplanation: Azure Policy initiatives let you assign a built-in regulatory compliance initiative (such as the ISO 27001/27002 initiative) at the subscription scope. Once assigned, the initiative automatically evaluates all new and existing resources against the standard's controls and flags any resource that is noncompliant, enforcing the required standard. Azure RBAC only manages who can perform actions on resources and has no role in evaluating configuration compliance against a standard. The regulatory compliance dashboard in Microsoft Defender for Cloud only displays compliance status for standards that have already been assigned via Azure Policy initiatives — it is a reporting view, not the mechanism that enforces the standard or triggers detection of noncompliant resources.

definition.stemRaw:
Your organization has a Microsoft Entra tenant that uses Microsoft Entra ID Governance. For each department, a dedicated catalog and set of access packages have been created to manage access to applications and data resources.  
  
You need to enable team leaders in each department to:  
  
- Add or remove access package assignments for the users in their department.  
- Ensure that the access packages do not appear in each user's My Access portal.  
  
The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
Which role should you assign to the team leaders?

finalExplanation: The Access Package Assignment Manager role is a built-in, least-privileged Microsoft Entra ID Governance role that allows a delegated user to view, add, and remove assignments for access packages they are authorized to manage, without granting broader catalog or access package management rights. Because assignments made through this role are performed directly by the delegated manager rather than through a user-initiated request, the access packages do not appear as requestable items in the affected users' My Access portal. This satisfies both requirements—managing assignments and keeping the packages hidden from My Access—while granting only the minimum permissions needed, unlike Identity Governance Administrator (too broad), Catalog Owner (manages the catalog and its resources/packages, not just assignments), or Access Package Manager (manages access package configuration/policies rather than solely assignments).

definition.stemRaw:
Your organization has a Microsoft 365 subscription with 1,000 users and a group named Group1. All users have Windows 11 devices and sign in using their Microsoft Entra accounts. The users do not have administrative rights on their devices.  
  
Members of Group1 remotely assist the users by taking control of their sessions. These remote control sessions run in the security context of the user being assisted.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that will:  
  
- Enable Group1 members to run apps that require administrative rights on the users' devices  
- Ensure the apps run in the context of each signed-in standard user  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Windows Local Administrator Password Solution (Windows LAPS)

definition.explanation:
Microsoft Intune Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM) allows administrators to define elevation rules for specific applications so that standard (non-admin) users can run those apps with elevated administrative rights, while the elevation is scoped to that application and executes in the context of the signed-in standard user rather than requiring a separate administrator account. This matches the requirement that apps run in the context of each signed-in standard user during remote-assistance sessions that operate under the user's own security context. Entra PIM provides just-in-time elevation for Entra/Azure directory roles, entitlement management automates access package requests/approvals for resources, and Windows LAPS manages local administrator account passwords — none of these enable per-app elevation for a standard user's own session.

**Learn more:** [What is Endpoint Privilege Management? - Microsoft Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/mem/intune/protect/epm-overview)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Intune Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM) allows administrators to define elevation rules for specific applications so that standard (non-admin) users can run those apps with elevated administrative rights, while the elevation is scoped to that application and executes in the context of the signed-in standard user rather than requiring a separate administrator account. This matches the requirement that apps run in the context of each signed-in standard user during remote-assistance sessions that operate under the user's own security context. Entra PIM provides just-in-time elevation for Entra/Azure directory roles, entitlement management automates access package requests/approvals for resources, and Windows LAPS manages local administrator account passwords — none of these enable per-app elevation for a standard user's own session.

definition.stemRaw:
You have a Microsoft Sentinel deployment.  
  
You are developing a solution to ensure that compliance with the MITRE ATT&CK framework is maintained as the framework evolves.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to identify which MITRE ATT&CK techniques are currently NOT addressed by the Microsoft Sentinel deployment.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: the Microsoft Sentinel Health Summary dashboard

finalExplanation: Microsoft Sentinel provides a dedicated MITRE ATT&CK coverage view (Threat management > MITRE ATT&CK) that maps every analytics rule to the tactics and techniques of the MITRE ATT&CK framework, presenting a heat-map/matrix where each cell shows how many active rules map to a given technique. Techniques with no active rules are visibly highlighted as uncovered, letting you search by technique name or ID and drill into related hunting queries to close the gap. This matrix is kept aligned with the current version of the MITRE ATT&CK framework, allowing ongoing compliance tracking as the framework evolves — which is exactly the requirement of identifying techniques not addressed by the deployment.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription that includes five Azure App Service instances hosting public web apps. Each instance is deployed across three Azure regions.  
  
The web apps process sensitive customer data and must be protected against common web exploits and malicious bots.  
  
You need to recommend a security solution that satisfies the following requirements:  
  
- Provides centralized management and updates for protection rules  
- Protects all the web apps without requiring changes to the application code  
- Minimizes costs  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

finalExplanation: Azure Front Door offers a global entry point with an integrated Web Application Firewall (WAF) that can be configured once as a centralized policy and applied across all backend web apps in every region, using Microsoft-managed rule sets for OWASP threats and bot protection that are updated automatically without needing to alter application code. Because the App Service instances span three regions, using a regional solution like Application Gateway would require deploying and maintaining separate WAF instances per region, increasing cost and management overhead — whereas Front Door's single global WAF policy meets the centralized management and cost-minimization requirements. Azure Firewall (network-layer) and Azure DDoS Protection (volumetric attack mitigation) do not provide web application-layer exploit and bot protection.

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription containing 100 virtual machines. The virtual machines run either Linux or Windows Server.  
  
You need to recommend a solution to discover which of the virtual machines are internet-facing.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?
definition.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud includes asset inventory and attack surface/attack path analysis capabilities that identify internet-facing virtual machines (for example, VMs with public IP addresses or exposed management ports) and generates recommendations such as 'Internet-facing virtual machines should be protected with network security groups.' This makes it the appropriate tool for discovering which VMs are exposed to the internet, unlike Defender for Cloud Apps (SaaS app discovery), Microsoft Sentinel (SIEM/SOAR log analytics), or Azure Network Watcher (network diagnostics without automated internet-exposure classification).

**Learn more:** [Protect your network resources - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/protect-network-resources) · [Identify and remediate attack paths - Microsoft Defender for Cloud](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/defender-for-cloud/how-to-manage-attack-path)

finalExplanation: Microsoft Defender for Cloud includes asset inventory and attack surface/attack path analysis capabilities that identify internet-facing virtual machines (for example, VMs with public IP addresses or exposed management ports) and generates recommendations such as 'Internet-facing virtual machines should be protected with network security groups.' This makes it the appropriate tool for discovering which VMs are exposed to the internet, unlike Defender for Cloud Apps (SaaS app discovery), Microsoft Sentinel (SIEM/SOAR log analytics), or Azure Network Watcher (network diagnostics without automated internet-exposure classification).

definition.stemRaw:
You have an on-premises application that processes Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and sends the data to Azure. The application includes the following components:  
  
- APIs that receive and send the PII  
- A data ingestion pipeline that stores the PII in an Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 account  
  
A compliance policy requires that all the PII data be encrypted by using encryption keys that are regularly rotated and stored in a central repository.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that adheres to the compliance policy. The solution must minimize administrative effort.  
  
Which two components should you include in the recommendation? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
(Choose two. Each correct selection is worth one point.)
definition.explanation:
Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 encrypts data at rest automatically through service-side encryption (SSE). To meet a compliance requirement for centrally stored, regularly rotated encryption keys with minimal administrative effort, you configure SSE to use customer-managed keys, and store and manage those keys in Azure Key Vault, which provides centralized storage, access control, and automated key rotation. TDE, Azure Disk Encryption, Cloud HSM, and Cloud PKI address different services (databases, VM disks, hardware key protection, and certificates respectively) and are not the appropriate mechanisms for encrypting Data Lake Storage Gen2 data at rest.

**Learn more:** [Azure Storage encryption for data at rest](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-service-encryption) · [Configure customer-managed keys for Azure Storage encryption](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/customer-managed-keys-configure-key-vault)

definition.stemRaw:
You have an Azure subscription containing 20 App Service web apps that provide services to external customers. Each web app has its own unique certificate and key.  
  
You need to recommend a solution for managing the keys and certificates of these web apps. The solution must meet the following requirements:  
  
- Provide a single tenancy to store the keys and certificates.  
- Maintain FIPS 140-2 Level 3 compliance.  
- Follow the principle of least privilege.  
- Minimize costs.  
- Minimize administrative effort.  
  
What should you include in the recommendation?

options: A single vault with role-based access control (RBAC) authorization
A single vault with vault access policy authorization
20 vaults with role-based access control (RBAC) authorization
20 vaults with vault access policy authorization

finalExplanation: Azure Key Vault Managed HSM is a fully managed, highly available, single-tenant HSM service — each Managed HSM instance is dedicated to a single customer, satisfying the single-tenancy requirement, unlike the multitenant Premium or Standard Key Vault SKUs. Managed HSM uses FIPS 140 Level 3 validated HSM hardware, meeting the required compliance level, whereas Key Vault Premium's HSM-backed keys are only validated to Level 2. A single Managed HSM instance can store all 20 web apps' unique keys and certificates, which minimizes both cost (one HSM pool instead of 20) and administrative overhead (one resource to manage instead of 20). Managed HSM's data plane exclusively uses Managed HSM local RBAC (it does not support the legacy access-policy model), which allows granular, per-key/per-principal role assignments that satisfy the principle of least privilege.

definition.stemRaw:
You manage several on-premises Hyper-V hosts running Windows Server virtual machines, and you also have an Azure subscription.  
  
You need to recommend a solution that uses Microsoft Sentinel to collect Security event logs from the virtual machines. The solution must:  
  
- Use the Windows Security Events via AMA data connector.  
- Collect only specific events.  
- Minimize costs.  
  
What should you recommend?  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1785478469753-1lrmq5hy.png)

blanks.label: In Azure, deploy:
options: Microsoft Defender for Cloud data collection settings

definition.explanation:
Data Collection Rules (DCRs) in Azure Monitor let you specify exactly which Windows Security event types (e.g., Common, Minimal, or Custom filtering) are collected via the Windows Security Events via AMA connector, allowing you to limit ingestion to only the required events and thereby control/minimize cost. Because the Hyper-V virtual machines are on-premises (not native Azure VMs), they must first be onboarded to Azure Arc by installing the Azure Connected Machine agent; this registers them as Arc-enabled servers so the Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) extension and the associated DCR can then be applied to them for log collection into Microsoft Sentinel.

**Learn more:** [Data collection rules in Azure Monitor](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/essentials/data-collection-rule-overview) · [Collect Windows Security Events using Azure Monitor Agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/data-connectors/windows-security-events-via-ama)
